docs.title: ns3-ntn-toolkit
docs.text:
An integrated ns-3.43 platform for 6G non-terrestrial networks: propagated LEO ephemerides, a measured 3GPP NR-NTN data plane, conditional handover, Space O-RAN control loops, sub-terahertz links and GPU ray tracing in one tree. Described in IEEE Open Journal of the Communications Society, 2026 (doi:10.1109/OJCOMS.2026.3745010).

Try it in the browser, no installation

The :material-satellite: Constellation demo on Hugging Face Spaces propagates real Starlink / OneWeb / Iridium NEXT / GPS TLEs in your browser using the same SGP4 backend the full toolkit uses. World map (Plotly · natural-earth), proper Earth-rotation-aware sub-satellite tracks, topocentric elevation/azimuth/range at any observer location.

# Python tooling, installable from PyPI
pip install ns3-ntn-toolkit              # metapackage
ns3-ntn-toolkit info                     # version + module list
14integrated ns-3 modules 0runnable examples 0O-RAN xApp actions recorded, no conflicts 0satellites in 32 s on a desktop

docs.title: Publication
docs.text:
The toolkit is described and evaluated in the following open-access article:

M. Uzair, B. G. Aldahlan, A. A. Albar, H. Althumali and A. Alghammas, "ns3-ntn-toolkit: An Integrated ns-3 Platform for 6G Non-Terrestrial Networks," IEEE Open Journal of the Communications Society, vol. 7, pp. 13440–13467, 2026, doi: 10.1109/OJCOMS.2026.3745010.

Fig. 1 of the article. The system the platform models. Height is altitude and link color is carrier. E2 reaches a satellite over the feeder bearer. The rail underneath shows the measurement path: packets leave an application, cross a modeled radio, and are read back at the sink, where every KPI is computed.

Over ten seeds, the measured cell reproduces the TR 38.821 zenith-to-edge decay to within 0.49 ± 1.30 dB, and a nadir-fixed beam follows the TR 38.811 pattern to 2.71 ± 0.21 dB RMS across a 39 dB excursion. A closed O-RAN control loop measures 104 ms end to end, 26 µs of it computation. In an archived geometry-driven scenario, the time-to-exit trigger removes every ping-pong and cuts handovers by 71 % against A3. The release cited in the article is v2.6.1.

docs.title: What is ns3-ntn-toolkit?
docs.text:
ns3-ntn-toolkit is an open-source ns-3 platform for 5G and 6G non-terrestrial network (NTN) research. Built on ns-3.43 with fourteen integrated modules, it models 3GPP Release-17/18/19 satellite networks end to end: propagated LEO ephemerides and TR 38.811 channels, Rel-17 conditional handover, an O-RAN near-RT RIC with xApps, NVIDIA Sionna ray tracing and sub-terahertz (100 GHz to 1 THz) propagation. Its KPIs (SINR, throughput, BLER, delay, jitter and loss) are measured from packets that cross the modeled radio rather than evaluated from closed-form expressions.

It is intended for research on LEO satellite networks, 5G NR-NTN, O-RAN over satellite, conditional handover, terahertz links, space-air-ground integrated networks, V2X over LEO, and AI/ML for satellite radio access networks.

The implementation follows 3GPP TR 38.811, TR 38.821, TS 38.213, TS 38.321, TS 38.331, TS 22.261 and TS 23.501; O-RAN E2AP, E2SM-KPM, E2SM-RC and A1; ITU-R P.676-13, P.618-13, P.838-3 and P.840; and SAE J2735 for vehicular messages.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
• :material-satellite-variant: Live constellations

    Full Vallado SGP4 for real Starlink, OneWeb, Kuiper, IRIS², Iridium NEXT and Telesat two-line elements. Walker-Star and Walker-Delta presets generate shells from orbital elements, which propagate on a Kepler plus J2 secular model because a generated shell has no TLE; the model reports which path a run took.

  • :material-radio-tower: 3GPP NR-NTN protocol stack

    TR 38.811 large-scale + small-scale fading. Rel-17 SIB19 + Timing Advance pre-compensation + UE GNSS location reporting + NTN-extended DRX + regenerative-vs-transparent payload. Conditional handover with TTE estimator.

  • :material-cogs: O-RAN Near-RT RIC + FlexRIC bridge

    xApps spanning beam management, slice orchestration, anomaly detection and predictive handover, on three RIC placements whose E2 latency comes from live slant geometry. E2AP, KPM and RC procedures run in-simulator over an ns-3 header with toolkit-internal type values; that is not ASN.1 APER over SCTP, and the FlexRIC bridge is the start of a wire-level path (its listener exchanges frame types and does not decode payloads yet).

  • :material-wave: Sub-THz physics (100 GHz to 1 THz)

    ITU-R P.676-13 line-by-line gaseous absorption over a layered atmosphere, P.618-13 scintillation, P.838-3 rain, P.840 fog. UM-MIMO, RIS quantisation sweep, ISAC CRB analysis.

  • :material-graph: AI/ML pipeline

    Stable-Baselines3 + PyTorch Geometric + ns3-gym. Pre-built environments for handover, beam management, slice orchestration, power control. Multi-agent baselines are single-agent PPO/SAC over N independent environment copies, not MAPPO/MASAC: there is no centralized critic and no inter-agent coupling.

  • :material-cube-outline: GPU ray tracing (NVIDIA Sionna RT)

    Optional GPU channel via Mitsuba 3 and TensorFlow, calibrated against the closed-form TR 38.811 reference. Every run prints whether its numbers were ray traced or fell back to free space, and a missing server can be made fatal rather than silent.

  • :material-airplane: SAGIN: HAPS + UAV + A2G

    20 km HAPS station-keeping, UAV mobility patterns, 3GPP TR 36.777 air-to-ground channel. Multi-layer routing: ground → UAV → HAPS → LEO.

  • :material-car-traction-control: V2X over LEO

    SUMO TraCI bridge for vehicular nodes consuming LEO connectivity in rural / oceanic / emergency scenarios.

  • :material-chart-line: Network slicing

    eMBB, URLLC and mMTC across LEO and GEO with per-5QI dedicated bearers. SLA percentiles come from a delay histogram, so a p99 is a percentile rather than a restated mean.

  • :material-monitor-dashboard: Observability stack

    InfluxDB + Grafana + NetSimulyzer 3D playback. Four pre-built Grafana dashboards. Per-slice / per-beam / per-cell KPI panels.

  • :material-earth: Live digital twin

    FastAPI prediction service, TLE refresh and a CesiumJS 3D viewer. Prediction and actuation share one guard implementation, so the twin and the simulation cannot drift apart.

  • :material-server: Reproducible infrastructure

    Docker compose for InfluxDB + Grafana, Docker compose for FlexRIC RIC + E2 Agent + xApps, every module with CMakeLists, every test gated.

Rel-17 conditional handover: TTE-aware candidate selection removes every ping-pong across a real LEO pass (ntn-cho). Space O-RAN: Near-RT RIC and on-board Space RIC over a 66-satellite constellation through feeder-link outages (oran-ntn). xApp control loop: 7,738 near-real-time decisions producing 71,967 recorded actions across 5 concurrent xApps, no conflicts (oran-ntn). Sub-THz beam tracking: EKF beam tracker holding a 100 GHz to 1 THz link through a LEO pass (thz-ntn). RL tooling: a training loop over a synthetic NTN environment and the ns3-ai shared-memory bridge (ns3-ai-ntn).

docs.title: Frequently asked questions
docs.text:
Which open-source ns-3 tools simulate LEO satellite and non-terrestrial networks?

ns3-ntn-toolkit is designed for this purpose. Unlike a single channel model or a flow-level LEO simulator, it integrates orbit propagation, 3GPP TR 38.811 channels, a real 5G NR data plane, Rel-17 conditional handover, an O-RAN Near-RT RIC, and sub-THz physics in one ns-3.43 distribution, so the complete non-terrestrial stack is simulated rather than a single layer.

How do I simulate 5G NR-NTN conditional handover (CHO) in ns-3?

Use the ntn-cho module. It implements the full 3GPP Rel-17/18 NTN CHO trigger set (measurement A3, location-based condEventD1, time-based condEventT1, timing-advance, elevation, and Rel-18 condEventD2), selectable in one example and executed over SGP4-propagated orbits with handovers driven by measured serving SINR. ./ns3 run "ntn-cho-real-stack --trigger=tte-aware".

Is there an open-source O-RAN simulator for non-terrestrial networks?

Yes. The oran-ntn module provides an O-RAN near-RT RIC and an on-board Space RIC with xApps, E2AP, KPM and RC procedures carried in-simulator over an ns-3 header, a FlexRIC bridge toward a wire-level E2AP path, and TS 28.552 KPM metrics measured at the PHY.

Can ns-3 simulate terahertz / sub-THz (100 GHz to 1 THz) satellite links?

Yes. The thz-ntn module implements ITU-R P.676-13 line-by-line molecular absorption over a layered atmosphere, P.618-13 tropospheric scintillation, P.838-3 rain and P.840 fog, plus RIS, ISAC and EKF beam tracking, as real ns-3 propagation-loss models chained onto the radio, so THz physics attenuate actual packets and show up in the measured SINR.

Does it support real Starlink / OneWeb / Iridium constellations?

Yes. ntn-constellation propagates real CelesTrak TLEs (Starlink, OneWeb, Kuiper, Iridium NEXT, Telesat) with a full Vallado SGP4 backend, and generates Walker-Delta / Walker-Star shells at any scale (a 1,584-satellite scenario runs in ~32 seconds on a desktop).

How is it different from SNS3, Hypatia, or other LEO network simulators?

SNS3 is DVB-S2/RCS2 (no NR), and Hypatia models flow-level routing and latency. ns3-ntn-toolkit adds the 3GPP 5G NR-NTN protocol stack, O-RAN control, conditional handover, sub-THz physics, Sionna ray tracing, and AI/ML hooks on top of real orbital mobility, and reuses SNS3's satellite channel where it helps. It targets protocol-level fidelity at constellation scale.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text: The architecture as published in the accompanying manuscript. Amber arrows follow one run left to right: orbit state, beam trigger, THz xApps, KPI export. Tone darkens with depth; a rounded outline marks a user-facing tool.

docs.title: The organising idea
docs.text:
Five layers sit on two vendored upstream stacks, which sit on an unmodified ns-3.43 core. Nothing in the core is patched, which is what makes the toolkit trackable against upstream ns-3 releases rather than a permanent fork.

The layering is not decorative. Each layer only knows about the one below it, so a scenario can replace a layer without the ones above noticing. The orbital layer does not know a radio exists. The radio does not know a RIC exists. The RIC gets its measurements through E2SM-KPM rather than by reaching into the PHY. This is what lets oran-ntn run over either radio backend, and what lets ntn-sionna substitute a ray-traced channel for a closed-form one without touching a scenario.

docs.title: The single most important property
docs.text:
The decision plane and the measurement plane are the same plane.

That sentence is doing real work. In a simulation, it is easy and common for a control decision to be evaluated against numbers that the decision could not have affected: a handover trigger that fires while a counter increments beside an unrelated SINR series. The result looks like a closed loop and is not one, and no amount of running it longer will reveal the gap.

Here, a trigger that fires calls into the RRC, which moves the terminal onto a different cell, whose SINR is then measured off the spectrum PHY by the same accumulator that fed the trigger. When that property fails somewhere, the toolkit says so in sim_health.csv rather than leaving it to be inferred.

docs.title: Orbital and mobility
docs.text:
ntn-constellation propagates the shell, from two-line elements or from orbital elements, and owns the contact graph over inter-satellite links including limb clearance. ntn-sagin adds the air and ground layers, UAV and HAPS, with a TR 36.777 channel. ntn-v2x puts vehicles under the shell with NR sidelink.

Everything above consumes one ephemeris, which is the reason coordinate frames agree: there is only one source of position.

docs.title: Protocol, L1 to L3
docs.text:
ntn-traffic is the spine. NtnRealStackHelper assembles a genuine NR cell, mmWave FR2 or 5G-LENA nr at FR1, under that ephemeris: SpectrumPhy, LDPC error model, HARQ, RLC, PDCP, RRC, EPC and GTP, with TR 38.811 NTN physics chained onto the channel and timers relaxed to the slant round trip.

ntn-cho decides when to hand over, ntn-rrc carries the SIB19 timing that makes uplink work over a round trip the terrestrial standard never anticipated, ntn-fapi exposes the MAC-PHY boundary, and ntn-slice differentiates the traffic across it.

docs.title: Physical layer
docs.text: thz-ntn and ntn-sionna both replace or augment the propagation chain rather than sitting beside it: a THz atmospheric term or a ray-traced channel impulse response attenuates real packets and shows up in the measured SINR.

docs.title: Control and learning
docs.text: oran-ntn closes the loop. E2SM-KPM indications carry measurements up, E2SM-RC control actions and A1 policies come back down, and the E2 latency between them is taken from live slant geometry, which is what makes the RIC placement question answerable. ns3-ai-ntn exposes the same loop to a Gymnasium agent over versioned shared memory.

docs.title: Operations
docs.text: ntn-observability records the scene once and exports it four ways. ntn-digital-twin runs the prediction outside the simulation and hands the schedule back in as a file that oran-ntn actuates; simulator state does not flow back into the twin.

docs.title: Where the boundaries are
docs.text:
An architecture page that only lists what is present is half a document. The toolkit's boundaries are stated in SCOPE_AND_LIMITATIONS.md, and the ones most likely to affect an experiment design are:

  • The air interface carries no propagation delay in the shipped runs; the NTN slant delay rides the transport leg, and the health record says so per row.
  • The multi-tap TR 38.811 NTN-TDL is not implemented; the measured channel carries large-scale loss with the spectrum model's own fading.
  • The in-simulation E2 transport is an ns-3 header, not ASN.1 APER over SCTP; the wire-level path is the FlexRIC bridge.
  • Release 19 AI/ML lifecycle management is absent entirely.

docs.text: This page walks you from a clean machine to a running 6G NTN simulation in under 30 minutes.

docs.title: Option 1 - Docker (fastest)
docs.text:
docker pull uzairdocker69/ns3-ntn-toolkit:latest
docker run --rm -it -p 8090:8090 -p 3000:3000 uzairdocker69/ns3-ntn-toolkit:latest

This gives you a shell inside a pre-built image with ns-3.43, all 14 contrib modules, and Python utilities ready. Port 8090 exposes the digital-twin FastAPI (that is the server's own default, see ntn_digital_twin/api/server.py); port 3000 exposes Grafana.

docs.title: ns3-ai-ntn - Reinforcement learning environments for NTN in ns-3
docs.text:
ns3-ai-ntn

A modernized ns3-ai bridge for ns-3.43: Gymnasium 1.0 over versioned shared memory, an AI-RAN inference contract, and NTN reinforcement-learning tooling

Toolkit  ·  Docs  ·  Install  ·  Results  ·  Examples

Source

This page mirrors contrib/ns3-ai-ntn/README.md. Figures are regenerated by the make_*.py scripts in contrib/ns3-ai-ntn/doc/figures/.

docs.title: Why this module
docs.text:
Reinforcement learning against a network simulator fails in two characteristic ways, and this fork fixes both. First, the agent may never be stepped: registering a Gymnasium interface without a Notify() call site gives a training loop that runs, converges and learns nothing. Second, the reward may be computed from state the action has not reached yet, which inverts it. On the original code a 5 to 15 dB improvement earned -15 while a 15 to 5 dB degradation earned -5, so the agent was paid more to make the link worse. The fix for the second is structural: the transition is latched inside GetObservation.

The C++ and Python sides share a protobuf schema over shared memory, a contract that used to be unchecked. The handshake now carries a protocol version, a module version and an FNV-1a schema digest, so a mismatch is reported instead of being misread as data. Upstream ns3-ai also crashed on NumPy 2.0, failed to import on Python 3.13 and lost pybind11 symbols under ns-3.43 link-time optimization; this fork fixes those and 8 other issues.

docs.title: System design
docs.text: Two processes and the bridge between them. The handshake is checked before the first step. The Gym path carries protobuf observations, actions and rewards; the message path carries fixed-layout structs and vectors; the AI-RAN inference contract runs over an in-process FIFO or length-prefixed TCP. Dashed boxes are offline or optional. Script: doc/figures/make_ns3_ai_ntn_design.py.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
(a) and (b): upstream ns3-ai benchmark on the RL-TCP example, 6 seeds, bars are means over seeds and whiskers the standard deviation across seeds; data in docs/benchmarking/gym-interface-data.m and docs/benchmarking/pure-cpp-data.m. (c): one 12 s run of oran-ntn-gym-handover-example in in-process mode (3 satellites, 2 UEs), parsed from the stored log toolkit-audit-2026-10-06/runs/A6-ai-twin-security/gym-inproc-12s/run.log. docs.title: Honest scope
docs.text:
• The four NTN environments in python_utils/ns3_ai_ntn (HandoverEnv, BeamMgmtEnv, SliceEnv, PowerCtrlEnv) are synthetic: they do not boot ns-3 and carry no measured KPI. They exercise the RL tooling. The environment that runs on a measured radio is OranNtnGymHandover in oran-ntn.
  • The bundled trainers are single-agent PPO and SAC over N independent environment copies. The MAPPO and MASAC wrappers share parameters but have no centralized critic and no joint observation; the agents cannot see or affect each other.
  • The inference contract mirrors the wire format a grpc++ server would expose, but the native grpc++ transport is not implemented yet; the runtimes behind it are deterministic mocks, not trained models.
  • 3GPP TR 38.843 AI/ML lifecycle management is not implemented.

docs.title: ntn-cho - Time-to-Exit Conditional Handover for LEO NTN
docs.text:
ntn-cho

Conditional handover for LEO: time-to-exit estimation from the ephemeris and the full standardized NTN trigger set

Toolkit  |  Docs  |  Install  |  Examples  |  Results

Source

This page mirrors contrib/ntn-cho/README.md. Figures are regenerated by the make_*.py scripts in contrib/ntn-cho/doc/figures/.

docs.title: Why this module
docs.text:
A LEO satellite is a cell that leaves. Terrestrial handover logic asks which neighbor looks best right now, and in orbit that question often answers itself wrongly: the best-looking neighbor is frequently the one about to set. This module estimates time to exit, how long a candidate will still be serviceable, from propagated orbits, and conditions the handover decision on it.

The standardized trigger set is implemented rather than approximated: TS 38.331 CondEvent A3, D1 on a fixed reference location, T1 on its absolute broadcast window, and Rel-18 D2 on a moving ephemeris reference, plus the elevation and timing-advance mechanisms that TR 38.821 studies. Each evaluates its own condition against live geometry, so they fire at different times. On the shipped two-cell pass, D2 and TA fired at 8 s, D1 at 69 s, A3 at 81 s, T1 at 125 s and elevation at 248 s, when the serving satellite finally reached the 10 degree floor.

A firing trigger does not always perform the cell change. ntn-cho-handover-traffic reports trigger-decided and fallback-decided handovers separately; on that pass five of the six classes fired without deciding a handover, because the vendored NR A3-RSRP and X2 machinery had already moved the terminal, and only D2 decided one. The counts are kept apart so that the CHO layer is never credited with a cell change the radio would have made on its own.

docs.title: System design
docs.text:
Figure 1. Classes of ntn-cho. The orbit predictor propagates the (optionally perturbed) ephemeris; the TTE estimator searches for each candidate's beam-exit instant; the measurement model and the measured SINR of a real NR NTN cell feed NtnChoAlgorithm, which executes on the cell and logs every decision. Source: ../media/ntn-cho/make_architecture.py.

Class Header Role NtnChoAlgorithm model/ntn-cho-algorithm.h Rel-17 CHO state machine (CHO_IDLE, CHO_PREPARED, CHO_CONDITION_MONITORING, CHO_EXECUTING, CHO_COMPLETED) with trigger classes TRIGGER_EVENT_A3, TRIGGER_LOCATION_D1, D2 (moving reference, TS 38.331 Section 5.5.4.15a), TRIGGER_TIME_T1, TRIGGER_ELEVATION, TRIGGER_TIMING_ADVANCE, TRIGGER_TTE_AWARE, TRIGGER_LTM_CONDITIONAL (Rel-19 conditional LTM), TRIGGER_TRAJECTORY_PREDICTIVE. combineWithA4 enforces the Rel-17 rule that T1, D1 and D2 are configured with the A4 leg. Optional RACH-less execution from ephemeris TA pre-compensation. GetMechanismStats() reports LTM switches, PCHO triggers, RACH-less and RACH executions, interruption. NtnTteEstimator model/ntn-tte-estimator.h Time to exit per candidate: a coarse forward scan brackets the exit, then a binary search refines it, both propagating the satellite through time (GetBeamSnapshotAtTime) rather than freezing it at Now(). NtnOrbitPredictor model/ntn-orbit-predictor.h Wraps SNS3 SGP4 mobility and antenna patterns to predict beam positions, coverage and best beams at future times. NtnMeasurementModel model/ntn-measurement-model.h TR 38.811 RSRP and SINR from satellite beams, with signed Doppler. NtnTr38811MobilityModel model/ntn-tr38811-mobility-model.h The TR 38.811 Section 6.1.1.1 UE classes (handheld, pedestrian, vehicular, HST, maritime, aviation, fixed IoT) as an ns-3 MobilityModel in ECEF, plus geodetic, elevation and slant utilities. NtnGeodeticFixedMobilityModel for fixed sites. NtnAiInterface model/ntn-ai-interface.h ns3-ai shared-memory bridge with a candidate-cell observation and action space (optional). NtnChoHelper, NtnRealisticMobilityHelper helper/ Wire a CHO scenario and aggregate KPIs; generate UE populations by TR 38.811 class.

Signaling scope. CHO is modeled at the decision and timing level. The radio underneath runs the mmwave ideal RRC (bearers set up synchronously) with no over-the-air conditional-reconfiguration PDU, and RACH is latency accounting: the interruption is priced as slant RTT plus processing (2d/c pre-compensation when RACH-less), not a PRACH Msg1 to Msg4 exchange. The core is the LTE EPC with real GTP-U, not a 5GC. Trigger classes and counters are exact and measured; the lower-layer handover protocol is abstracted.

docs.title: Handover rate of the exit-triggered rule
docs.text:
Figure 3. Handover rate under line of sight on a 550 km, 53 deg Walker shell (phasing F = 17). (a) Against the number of satellites at 30 deg N; (b) against terminal latitude for 1584 satellites. Lines: analysis; open markers: exact-geometry Monte Carlo; filled markers: ns-3 with ntn-cho-tte-campaign, fresh seeds 11 to 20, 1200 s horizon, 95 % intervals.

From the November 2026 campaign of examples/ntn-cho-tte-campaign.cc (all runs from one recorded binary and frozen libraries; code and data in the toolkit workspace under paper/taes-2026-cho-ephemeris/, runs_nov/ with PROVENANCE.txt, analysis in analysis_nov/ and analysis_rate/): the exit-triggered maximum-service-time rule handed over 0.242 ± 0.004 times per terminal-minute in ns-3 against 0.234 in the exact-geometry Monte Carlo, and the nearest-satellite rule 0.826 against 0.847. The Poisson pass model overstated Walker rates by 4 to 18 percent for shells with enough satellites in view.

docs.text:
./test.py -s ntn-cho
./test.py -s ntn-standards-validation
  • ntn-cho registers 35 test cases: the algorithm and state machine, D2 trigger, A4 combination and time to trigger, slant-based RACH interruption, RACH-less execution and its timing advance, the standardized triggers, T1 as an absolute window, LTM cadence, TTE estimation and its sigma propagation under ephemeris error, orbit-predictor time offsets and accuracy, exit-triggered selection, and well-formed handover CSVs.
  • ntn-standards-validation registers 4: SGP4 against Kepler theory, the zenith-pass Doppler envelope, ENU pass geometry, and the elevation and slant relation (about 1932 km at 10 deg for LEO-600).

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text:
• Required: ns-3.43 and the SNS3 satellite module (NtnOrbitPredictor uses its SGP4 mobility and antenna patterns); toolkit module ntn-rrc (linked by CMakeLists.txt).
  • Examples: ntn-traffic (NtnRealStackHelper, NtnRealisticTrafficHelper), ntn-constellation (Sgp4MobilityModel, WalkerConstellation), the toolkit's mmwave and lte.
  • Optional: ns3-ai or ns3-ai-ntn, only for NtnAiInterface.

docs.title: Scope and limitations
docs.text:
• Decision and timing level CHO over an ideal RRC; no over-the-air conditional reconfiguration and no PRACH procedure (see the signaling note above).
  • On short two-cell passes the vendored NR A3 and X2 handover can move the terminal before a CHO trigger trips; read the trigger-decided count, not the total.
  • ntn-cho-tte-campaign is a system-level simulation in the TR 38.821 Section 6.1 sense: link budget per terminal and satellite on the ns-3 event queue, not a packet-level PHY.
  • The elevation and TA mechanisms are TR 38.821 study items, not standardized CondEvents.

docs.title: ntn-constellation
docs.text:
title: ntn-constellation - LEO Walker generation, orbital propagation & contact-graph routing description: ns-3 module for non-terrestrial networks: Walker-Delta/Star LEO constellations, SGP4/J2 orbital propagation, ISL contact-graph routing, and live TLE feeds.

ntn-constellation

LEO shells from element sets or Walker parameters, propagated inside ns-3, with a contact graph and routing over inter-satellite links

Toolkit  |  Docs  |  Install  |  Examples  |  Results

Source

This page mirrors contrib/ntn-constellation/README.md. Figures are regenerated by the make_*.py scripts in contrib/ntn-constellation/doc/figures/.

docs.title: Why this module
docs.text:
Every layer above this one needs to know where the satellites are, and it needs the same answer at every layer. ntn-constellation builds a shell from two-line element sets or from Walker parameters, propagates it during Simulator::Run(), and hands one ephemeris to the radio, the handover logic, the routing and the visualization. On top of the geometry sits a network view: a contact graph over ground and inter-satellite links, with limb clearance so that a link which would graze the atmosphere is never offered, and path computation that ranges from plain shortest delay to a lifetime-aware search that prefers routes which will last.

The free-space link budget is checked against the TR 38.821 corpus rather than against itself. That distinction has a history here: an earlier calibration test compared the reference corpus with a synthetic offset of itself and never touched the toolkit.

docs.title: System design
docs.text:
Figure 1. Classes of ntn-constellation and how they connect. Element sets or a Walker configuration feed Sgp4MobilityModel; the contact-graph scheduler turns positions into link up and down events; the router installs the chosen path as IPv4 host routes on point-to-point links whose delay follows the live range. Source: ../media/ntn-constellation/make_architecture.py.

Everything lives in the ns3::ntncon namespace.

Header Key types Role walker-constellation.h WalkerConfig, WalkerConstellation Walker-Delta and Walker-Star generation (BuildDelta, BuildStar): planes, satellites per plane, phasing, altitude, inclination. orbital-elements.h TleRecord, KeplerianElements TLE parsing with checksums, classical elements. sgp4-mobility-model.h Sgp4MobilityModel ns-3 MobilityModel for one satellite. Default backend: analytic Kepler with secular J2 on RAAN and argument of perigee. SetUseVallado(true) switches a TLE-sourced orbit to full Vallado SGP4 (drag term included); Walker elements always use the Kepler + J2 path, and IsUsingSgp4() reports which one is running. ECEF, ECI and geodetic accessors, GetElevationDeg(), SetSimulationEpochUnix() for a common time origin. contact-graph-scheduler.h ContactGraphScheduler, ContactEvent Ground-to-satellite and satellite-to-satellite visibility over time, limb clearance, range caps; raises up, down and update events and counts them per link class. contact-graph-router.h ContactGraphRouter Path computation over the time-varying graph: BFS, weighted Dijkstra, ShortestPathCost with a caller-supplied edge cost, LifetimeAwarePath, and a regenerative-only transit filter (SetRegenMode). Returns node-ID vectors; it installs no forwarding table itself. ntn-visibility-index.h NtnVisibilityIndex Exact argmax-elevation lookup by branch and bound, the same satellite a brute-force scan would choose, without the satellites x terminals loop. ntn-sat-link-error-model.h NtnSatLinkErrorModel Per-packet error model for GSL and ISL hops: Es/N0 from the live slant range, mapped through a DVB-S2 MODCOD waterfall to a block error probability. ntn-xn-handover.h, ntn-xnap-messages.h NtnXnHandover, NtnXnapHeader The TS 38.300 Section 9.2.3 Xn sequence between two regenerative satellites, carried over the ISL. tr38821-corpus.h Tr38821CorpusReader, CalibrationHarness TR 38.821 Set-1 and Set-2 reference budgets plus a Starlink latency corpus, with residuals against the toolkit's own predictions.

Two propagators, two fidelity levels. In C++, Kepler + J2 is the default and full SGP4 is opt-in for real element sets. The Python companion (ntn_constellation, below) always uses the sgp4 library and Skyfield, so "SGP4" in this README means the Python side or a C++ satellite with SetUseVallado(true).

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
The figures and numbers below come from the route-break study built on this module (paper/taes-2026-route-breaks/: code and data). Every number is read from its stored outputs (out/p7_v8.jsonl, out/p7_v9.jsonl and the law checks), produced by examples/ntn-constellation-route-lifetime.cc through the campaign drivers in that folder. Setup: Starlink (72 x 22, 550 km, 53 deg), Kuiper (34 x 34, 630 km, 51.9 deg) and OneWeb (12 x 49, 1200 km, 87.9 deg) shells with +Grid laser links, plus real Starlink and OneWeb shells from CelesTrak element sets of 2 October 2026; gateway pairs London and New York, Sydney and Los Angeles; every link a 100 Mb/s IPv4 point-to-point link that drops all packets while its contact is down; one 20 packet/s UDP flow for 45 min per run.

Figure 2. Ground-link acquisitions per hour against mean delay stretch for five route recomputation families on the development shells, means over 6 start instants. Each line is one family as its budget, window or weight varies; the grey line is the longest-pass floor on any policy that switches before its route breaks.

Figure 3. Packet loss of reactive routing (on demand, and snapshot routing every 1 s) measured in ns-3 against the loss predicted from a route trace taken at other start instants. Hollow markers: development cells; filled: held-out cells, with the range over runs.

Measured quantity Value Largest +Grid inter-plane range, Starlink / Kuiper / OneWeb development shells 1972 / 1317 / 1983 km, against a 5000 km cap Largest range over every phasing factor, same shells 2353 / 2284 / 2196 km Inter-satellite link drops recorded by the scheduler 0 in 828 packet-level runs; 0 in all 3352 lattice runs Packet loss, on-demand routing / 1 s snapshot routing 1.35 % / 1.65 % Error of predicted cell-mean loss, development cells median 2.2 %, largest 4.6 % Error of predicted cell-mean loss, held-out cells median 2.9 %, largest 9.6 % Loss with one terminal per gateway: lifetime search (budget 0.05) / merged snapshots (120 s) / on demand 0.70 % / 0.82 % / 1.35 % Ground-link acquisitions relative to the lifetime search, real orbits: elevation ranking / ISASR 1.05 to 1.13 times / 1.63 to 2.18 times

What these say about the module: with range-limited +Grid links on these shells, every forced route change the scheduler logged was a ground link setting, so the contact graph and the ISL range law did their job, and the loss of reactive routing could be predicted from a route trace without a fitted parameter. The margin of the lifetime search is modest: merged snapshots traded places with it depending on the delay metric. The study ran on the copy of this module recorded in paper/taes-2026-route-breaks/ns3_patch/; make_macros_corr.py and make_figs.py there regenerate every number and figure from out/.

docs.text:
Inside the toolkit, where the module is already present and built:

./ns3 run "ntn-constellation-route-lifetime --policy=life --eps=0.05"
./test.py -s ntn-constellation

Standalone, into an existing ns-3.43 tree:

git clone -b ntn-constellation-v2 https://github.com/Muhammaduazir69/ntn-constellation.git contrib/ntn-constellation
./ns3 configure --enable-examples --enable-tests

INSTALL.md lists the dependencies. The two access-link examples build on ntn-traffic (the toolkit's real NR stack) and on ntn-cho (TR 38.811 terminal classes), so the toolkit tree is the easiest place to run them.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Binaries land in build/contrib/ntn-constellation/examples/ as ns3.43-<name>-default.

Example What it shows Command ntn-constellation-walker-traffic A Walker-Delta shell gives the contact-graph context while one serving satellite carries a real mmwave NR NTN cell (NtnRealStackHelper) to TR 38.811 ground terminals at its sub-point. SINR, TBLER and throughput come off the PHY trace. ./ns3 run "ntn-constellation-walker-traffic --simSeconds=20 --numPlanes=4 --satsPerPlane=11 --altKm=550 --inclinationDeg=53" ntn-constellation-sgp4-mobility-traffic One LEO satellite from a TLE drives a real NR cell; the scheduler tracks GSL up and down from the live geometry. Without --gsLat/--gsLon the ground station sits under the satellite's t=0 sub-point, so a pass always happens. ./ns3 run "ntn-constellation-sgp4-mobility-traffic --simSeconds=20 --tle=contrib/ntn-rrc/data/iss-zarya.tle" ntn-constellation-isl-routed-traffic GS1 -> satA -> ISL -> satB -> GS2 with real IPv4 forwarding through the satellites, per-hop delay from the live range and a contact gate per hop. Delay, jitter and loss are measured at NtnOranSink from the in-band header. ./ns3 run "ntn-constellation-isl-routed-traffic --duration=40" ntn-constellation-real-routed The routing decision installs IPv4 static routes, and the flow reroutes from satA to satB when satA sets and satB rises (two Walker neighbors projected into a local ENU frame). ./ns3 run "ntn-constellation-real-routed --duration=40" ntn-constellation-route-lifetime Ground-to-ground routing over a +Grid shell under the recomputation policies of the route-break study (snap, ondemand, asr, asrk, life, elev, elevb, track, alpr, isasr). Every link drops packets while down, so the cost of a stale route is measured. Real shells via --tle, --edges, --epochUnix. ./ns3 run "ntn-constellation-route-lifetime --policy=life --eps=0.05"

Each example writes sim_health.csv to --outputDir (where it has one) and prints a measured summary on stdout. The walker and SGP4 examples need the toolkit's mmwave module; the routed examples need only core ns-3 plus ntn-traffic and ntn-cho.

docs.title: Python companion
docs.text:
The ntn_constellation package (pip install -e . in this directory) is the tool-side pipeline: fresh element sets from CelesTrak or Space-Track with an on-disk cache, canonical SGP4/SDP4 through sgp4 and Skyfield, presets (Starlink, OneWeb, Kuiper, Telesat Lightspeed, Iridium NEXT), Walker generators that emit valid TLEs, ISL topology builders, and exporters for the SNS3 scenario layout and CesiumJS CZML. It does not touch the C++ build.

python3 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install -e .[test]
.venv/bin/ntn-fetch kuiper --out data/kuiper --isl-walker --czml       # preset, no network
.venv/bin/ntn-fetch starlink --out data/starlink-now --max-sats 200 --czml   # live CelesTrak

Against an independent Skyfield reference it showed 0 NaN over 24 h, 66 satellites and 1440 samples, and a largest error of 23.5 us over an 1800 s STARLINK-1008 pass (tests/).

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
./test.py -s ntn-constellation

test/ntn-constellation-test-suite.cc registers 36 test cases: TLE parsing and checksums, periodic return, ECEF altitude and the geocentric contract of Sgp4MobilityModel, Vallado SGP4 verification and its offset from Kepler + J2 on a real LEO element set, Walker-Delta geometry, contact scheduling (LEO pass, ISL pair, gate hysteresis, range updates, limb clearance, contact-end prediction, ISL candidates), the router (direct edges, BFS, weighted Dijkstra, regenerative-only paths, LifetimeAwarePath, several under Simulator::Run()), NtnVisibilityIndex against brute force, the Xn handover procedure, the satellite link error model, and the TR 38.821 and Starlink calibration harness. The orbit models are also checked against Kepler theory, the Doppler envelope and TR 38.821 geometry by ntn-standards-validation in ntn-cho.

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text:
• ns-3.43 with core and mobility; satellite (SNS3) and thz-ntn are linked by the module's CMakeLists.txt.
  • Examples: ntn-traffic (NR stack, NtnOranApplication), ntn-cho (TR 38.811 terminals, ENU projection), the toolkit's mmwave.
  • Python companion: Python 3.10+, sgp4, skyfield (see pyproject.toml).

docs.title: Scope and limitations
docs.text:
• The C++ default is Kepler + J2 secular, accurate to a few km over hours for near-circular LEO shells; drag enters only through SetUseVallado(true) on a TLE-sourced satellite.
  • ContactGraphRouter computes paths; examples install them. Nothing in the module writes an ns-3 forwarding table by itself.
  • RegenMode filters transit nodes and, through NtnXnHandover, decides whether a satellite may run an Xn handover. It does not build a gNB on the satellite. The XnAP messages are an ns-3 Header with toolkit-internal type values, not ASN.1 APER with TS 38.423 procedure codes.
  • Contact-graph routing follows CCSDS concepts; there is no bundle protocol.

docs.text:
title: ntn-digital-twin - live LEO constellation mirror with handover prediction API description: ns-3 NTN digital twin: pulls live CelesTrak TLEs, propagates with SGP4, and serves a FastAPI handover-prediction REST API for any satellite ground location.

ntn-digital-twin

A live constellation twin that predicts handovers from ephemeris and hands the schedule to a running ns-3 simulation, which actuates it

Toolkit  ·  Docs  ·  Install  ·  Results  ·  Examples

Source

This page mirrors contrib/ntn-digital-twin/README.md. Figures are regenerated by the make_*.py scripts in contrib/ntn-digital-twin/doc/figures/.

docs.title: Why this module
docs.text: A digital twin that only predicts is a dashboard. This one propagates two-line elements, evaluates a handover guard, and exports the decisions to a running ns-3 simulation, where the handover either happens or does not. Prediction and actuation share one guard implementation. They used to be two copies of the same logic in two languages, and extracting them into one evaluator exposed three places where they had quietly diverged: the ranking quantity was not the comparison quantity, initial acquisition was counted as a handover, and the time-to-trigger window did not restart when the best target changed. Both paths now compare a dB link-budget margin rather than topocentric degrees.

docs.title: System design
docs.text:
The twin sync loop. Inputs on the left, the Python service in the middle, consumers on the right. The red dashed path (ns-3 state back into the twin) is not implemented. Script: doc/figures/make_ntn_digital_twin_design.py.

The loop, every --interval seconds:

  1. Fetch TLEs from CelesTrak through a 6 h on-disk cache, or, for a deterministic run, generate Walker elements on the epoch the ns-3 scenario uses.
  2. Propagate the constellation with SGP4 (ntn-constellation, raw Satrec).
  3. Write CZML for a Cesium viewer and line protocol (ntn_sat_pos, the ntn-observability schema) for InfluxDB and Grafana.
  4. Optionally write the handover schedule with emit_predictions_file: an epoch_unix header, then t_s,ueId,recommendedGnbId,confidence lines, where t_s is seconds from the shared epoch (equal to ns-3 simulation time) and recommendedGnbId is 1-indexed in the order the ns-3 scenario builds its E2 nodes.

On the ns-3 side, OranNtnTwinPredictionConsumer in oran-ntn loads the file and, at each t_s whose confidence clears a floor, fires a HANDOVER_TRIGGER into the E2 and CHO loop, or calls NtnRealStackHelper::TriggerHandover directly. A failed iteration is logged and the next one runs on schedule.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
One deterministic twin run (Walker source, 66 satellites in 6 planes of 11 at 53 degrees, observer 33.68 N 73.05 E, 2700 s horizon, 10 s step), artifacts written 6 Oct 2026: toolkit-audit-2026-10-06/runs/A6-ai-twin-security/twin-walker/ (twin-orbits.tle, twin-pred.txt, twin.czml, twin.lp). Panel (b) is the 5 min CZML window at loop time, 30 s samples. Script: doc/figures/make_ntn_digital_twin_results.py.

The twin exported 5 handovers in 45 minutes, at 280, 610, 1100, 1650 and 2180 s, each to a different satellite, with confidence between 0.13 and 0.23 (the elevation margin over the runner-up divided by 30 degrees, clipped to [0, 1]). The first serving satellite is not listed because initial acquisition is not a handover. The CZML and line protocol hold one record per satellite (66 each), which is what the Cesium viewer and the Grafana dashboards read.

Verification figures quoted in earlier releases (a 144-iteration compressed 24 h loop with 0 errors and 0 m position error against direct SGP4, and a /predict/handover p99 of 29.9 ms over 100 calls for 50 satellites and a 10 min horizon) come from a verification run whose raw log is not stored in the tree. test_api_predict_handover_under_500ms and test_run_iteration_handles_missing_network check the bounds that matter on every test run.

docs.text:
Inside the toolkit:

Standalone:

docs.text:
This module has no ns-3 C++ examples; its entry points are the two CLIs and the prediction file.

Entry point What it does ntn-twin-loop runs the refresher; --czml, --lp (or UDP), --max-sats, --interval, --max-iterations ntn-twin-api serves the REST API on port 8090 emit_predictions_file(...) docs.text:
cd contrib/ntn-digital-twin && pytest tests/ -v   # 28 tests in 5 files
./test.py -s ntn-digital-twin                      # 2 C++ cases (TWIN-02)
File Tests Covers tests/test_twin_loop.py 8 line-protocol schema, network outages without a crash, API health, state, latency under 500 ms, response schema, A3 hysteresis against bare argmax, Walker source on the shared epoch tests/test_twin04_a3_guard.py 8 slant range, dB SNR, A3 offset and minimum-service dwell, predictions emitted only when configured, exporter and REST agree event for event tests/test_twin04_shared_guard.py 10 ranking quantity equals comparison quantity, initial acquisition is not a handover, time-to-trigger restarts on a new target, minimum service and minimum elevation, run_a3 matches stepping by hand tests/test_wsc_predictions_export.py 1 the prediction file format the C++ loader parses tests/test_gate9_twin_sim_agreement.py 1 twin serving selection against Skyfield geometry on the same orbits

The C++ case "ns-3 replays the twin's orbits" loads the twin's TLEs into Sgp4MobilityModel, walks the window inside Simulator::Run() and compares handover instants. It runs only when NTN_TWIN_ARTIFACT_DIR points at a directory holding twin-orbits.tle and twin-pred.txt (for example the twin-walker run above); otherwise it returns without asserting.

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text: Python 3.10 or newer, the sibling ntn-constellation Python package (SGP4), FastAPI 0.110 or newer, Uvicorn, Pydantic v2, requests; pytest and httpx for the tests, Skyfield for the gate-9 test. The C++ half needs ns-3.43 core and mobility and ntn-constellation. See INSTALL.md.

docs.title: Honest scope
docs.text:
• The twin is a standalone constellation mirror. It consumes live TLEs (or a deterministic Walker source) and serves REST, CZML and line protocol; it does not ingest ns-3 state. Sim-to-twin mirroring is not implemented.
  • Twin-to-sim is implemented: the prediction file is actuated by OranNtnTwinPredictionConsumer in oran-ntn.
  • Gate 9 compares the twin's closed-form elevation with Skyfield over the same Python-propagated orbits. That is a geometry check, close to a tautology, not a twin-versus-simulator check. The C++ TWIN-02 case is the one that compares with ns-3, and it needs the twin artifacts to run. Its agreement is expected to be below 1, because the twin applies an A3 guard while the replay uses bare argmax elevation.
  • The viewer patch was written against a CesiumJS page that has since been retired; it remains as the reference integration.

docs.title: ntn-fapi
docs.text:
A Small Cell Forum FAPI MAC-PHY adapter on a live NR service access point, with a latency figure that says what it does not contain

Toolkit  ·  Docs  ·  Install  ·  Examples  ·  Results

docs.title: Why this module
docs.text:
FAPI is the interface between MAC and PHY that real base stations are built on. The reason to model it in a simulator is to ask what an NTN round trip does to a slot pipeline designed for a terrestrial one, and that question needs messages produced by a real scheduler at real slot timing, not structs filled on a timer.

ntn-fapi gives ns-3 the SCF-222 message vocabulary and a bridge that decorates the live mmwave MAC-PHY service access point (SAP). SLOT.indication fires at the radio's own cadence, DL_TTI.request comes from real downlink allocations, and CRC.indication carries the real per-TB decode outcome. HARQ state is keyed by frame, subframe, slot and RNTI, because keying by slot alone let two terminals in the same slot overwrite each other.

One point the module states rather than implies: the backend it decorates has no propagation delay model, so the measured request-to-indication interval is a slot-pipeline turnaround and not an NR-NTN one. The bridge probes the channel and labels the value measured-no-air-propagation, and the test gate asserts that the mean stays below the geometric one-way floor of the configured link.

docs.title: System design
docs.text: Figure 1. NtnFapiSapBridge interposes two forwarding decorators between an already-wired MmWaveEnbMac and MmWaveEnbPhy. Every SAP call is forwarded unchanged; the FAPI struct is recorded as a side effect, so the bridge observes the slot timing without perturbing it. The reverse path (RX_DATA.indication, CRC.indication) is fed from the PHY reception trace, where the mmwave error model has already decided the TB. Source: doc/figures/make_architecture.py.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
The figure and table below are built from stored runs of the shipped examples, made during the toolkit audit of 6 October 2026 (ns-3-dev/toolkit-audit-2026-10-06/runs/A1-cho-rrc-fapi/). Each configuration ran once for 5 simulated seconds with 4 UEs on the default 2.185 GHz, 20 MHz mmwave NTN cell. The script that reads them is doc/figures/make_results.py.

Figure 2. (a) Latency read off the MAC-PHY SAP in ntn-fapi-real-stack (4948 SFN/slot-matched DL_TTI.request and CRC.indication pairs; the range bar spans min to max) against the one-way propagation floor that the link geometry implies. (b) FAPI data slots per run, split by the CRC outcome that the measured PHY decode produced, with the measured mean DL SINR and TBLER of each run.

Run (5 s, 4 UEs) Measured SINR (dB) Measured TBLER Data slots sent CRC pass HARQ retx TX_DATA.request PHY TBs (phy_rx_tb) ntn-fapi-dl-data-slotloop, seed 1 19.78 0.031 4948 4782 166 19094 19094 ntn-fapi-dl-data-slotloop, --RngRun=2 20.26 0.044 4736 4523 213 19041 19041 ntn-fapi-leo-pass-slotloop, ISS TLE 23.99 0.010 4759 4645 114 18894 18894 ntn-fapi-real-stack, seed 1 19.78 0.031 4948 4782 166 not printed 19094

What the data say:

  • TX_DATA.request equals the PHY's own TB count in every run that prints both. A free-running slot loop could not produce that identity; it is the check that the messages come from the SAP.
  • The SAP turnaround (DL_TTI.request to CRC.indication) had a mean of 643.8 us, min 535.7 us and max 732.1 us; the scheduler pipeline (DL_TTI.request to SLOT.indication) averaged 552.2 us. Both sit well below the 1834.6 us one-way floor derived from the geometry, which is the arithmetic sign that no air propagation is in them (fapi_sap.csv, air_propagation_present = 0).
  • ntn-fapi-real-stack and ntn-fapi-dl-data-slotloop at seed 1 produced identical radio numbers: both ride the same cell recipe and differ only in what they print.
  • --scsKhz changes the FAPI-side slot label only. The 15 kHz audit run (fapi-dl-scs15) reproduced the 30 kHz numbers exactly, because the mmwave cell keeps its own numerology.

docs.title: Scope and limitations
docs.text:
• The structs are a source-level C++ model with SCF field names. They use std::vector and std::variant, have no fixed byte layout and are not serialized, so they are not a drop-in ABI for NVIDIA Aerial cuPHY or OAI nFAPI.
  • The decorated mmwave channel has no propagation delay model, so the SAP latency excludes the NTN round trip. Read it as a slot-pipeline turnaround.
  • In the stored example runs UL_TTI.request carried no grant (20000 requests, 0 with a grant), since those scenarios carry downlink traffic; the uplink path is exercised by the unit test.

ntn-observability

docs.title: Why this module
docs.text: A multi-hour, multi-satellite run produces the telemetry a real RAN does (SINR, TBLER, goodput, timing advance, satellite positions, handovers), but ns-3's default trace surface stops at flat ASCII files. Visualizing an orbital simulation is also a question of what you refuse to draw: a globe that shows satellites moving is easy, while one that shows which satellite actually serves which terminal, at a time that maps back to simulation time, is the one that can catch a bug. This module records the scene once and exports it to the tools operators already use, with links traveling alongside positions, labels escaped on the way out, and a manifest that makes each run reproducible.

docs.title: System design
docs.text: Measured sources on the left, the recording core in the middle, sinks and external tools on the right. The schema names every measurement once; tools/check_dashboard_producers.py traces each Grafana panel back to the code that emits it. Script: doc/figures/make_ntn_observability_design.py.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
One run of ntn-observability-traffic (60 s, 550 km SGP4 pass, 20 GHz, 85 dBm EIRP, seed 1), plotted from the line-protocol file the sink wrote rather than from simulator memory: sweep-results-2026-06-25/ntn-observability/traffic-heavy.lp in the toolkit workspace (59 points, 58 with a PHY sample). Script: doc/figures/make_ntn_observability_results.py.

Read back from the export: elevation 89.2 to 51.3 degrees, slant range 550 to 688 km, mean per-second SINR 25.08 dB, mean per-second goodput 4.84 Mb/s. The run's own health record (traffic-heavy-out/sim_health.csv, all rows passing) gives the whole-run values: 26,119 transport blocks received, SINR 24.96 dB, TBLER 0.033, 4.71 Mb/s throughput, 7.81 ms one-way delay from in-band timestamps, 3.3 % application loss. Goodput eases from about 4.9 to 4.5 Mb/s over the last 20 s as the slant range grows; the plot is drawn from the exported series, not from a separate log.

Also stored from the same sweep: ntn-netsimulyzer-official-demo (6 SGP4 satellites, 4 TR 38.811 UEs, 15 s) wrote a NetSimulyzer scene with 190 events, a CZML file and a manifest that round-trips (netsim-scene.log: mean DL SINR 17.34 dB, TBLER 0.041, 16.58 Mb/s).

docs.title: ntn-rrc
docs.text: title: ntn-rrc - 3GPP NR-NTN RRC procedures (SIB19, timing advance, DRX) description: ns-3 module implementing 3GPP Rel-17 NR-NTN RRC for satellite networks: SIB19 ephemeris broadcast, ephemeris-driven timing advance, pass-aware DRX, GNSS reporting.

docs.title: ntn-rrc
docs.text:
NR-NTN control plane for ns-3: SIB19 ephemeris that a UE actually decodes, payload-aware timing advance, and DRX that gates a real flow

Toolkit  ·  Docs  ·  Install  ·  Examples  ·  Results

docs.title: Why this module
docs.text:
NR works over a satellite because three timing mechanisms absorb a round trip the terrestrial standard never planned for: a broadcast K_offset that shifts the uplink grant, a timing advance that pre-compensates propagation, and a validity duration after which the terminal must read SIB19 again. Each is useful only if something downstream consumes it. Stock ns-3 has none of them.

ntn-rrc adds them and wires them to consumers. The SIB19 broadcaster fills NTN-Config-r17 from a real orbit and quantizes it to the TS 38.331 field steps; a UE-side pre-compensator decodes it, propagates the satellite with a chosen orbit model and forms its own timing advance; the scheduler in the sibling ntn-traffic module can read the broadcast cellSpecificKoffset. Timing advance includes the feeder leg for a transparent payload, so the payload mode is not a label: in the shipped test geometry the transparent advance is 8.0 ms longer, twice 1200 km over c. DRX gates a real flow rather than scaling a measured goodput afterwards.

docs.title: System design
docs.text: Figure 1. Classes and data flow. Orbit and terminal mobility (SGP4 from ntn-constellation, TR 38.811 UE classes from ntn-cho, an optional gateway for the feeder leg) feed the timing advance; the broadcaster turns it into SIB19 content, the codec serializes it, and the UE-side pre-compensator decodes it. Cross-module hooks reach the uplink scheduler (K_offset) and the PHY trace (measured SINR) of the ntn-traffic radio stack. Source: doc/figures/make_architecture.py.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
The numbers below come from an uplink timing pre-compensation study run with this module's ntn-rrc-ul-timing example (NtnSib19Broadcaster plus NtnUlTimingPrecompensator on SGP4 orbits). The study binary is that example with one addition that is not yet merged here: SIB19 content announced 0.64 s ahead of its epoch (--leadS), as the si-Periodicity requires. The patch, its regression check and the campaign scripts are in paper/tvt-2026-uplink-timing/ of the toolkit tree (ns3_patch/, run_ns3_campaign.py, make_macros.py).

Experiment. 400 LEO passes, 100 on each of four shells drawn from real element sets (357, 470 and 571 km Starlink shells, 1201 km OneWeb), with the closest approach drawn uniformly over a day, a 900 s window around it, a 25 degree elevation mask and 3 m GNSS error. Every scheme runs on the same passes (paired design, one noise seed per pass). The timing error limit is T_e' = 456 ns, the 716 ns NTN limit of TS 38.133 minus a 260 ns implementation allowance.

Figure 2. Timing error against information age on the 470 km shell. (a) UE-side error for four propagators: closed-form bound (lines), Monte Carlo 99th percentile (filled) and ns-3 99th percentile (hollow, pooled over 40 passes). (b) Common-delay error with the gateway as reference point: Taylor coefficients against age; economized and window-fit coefficients against the validity window. Dotted red lines mark T_e and T_e'.

Figure 3. ns-3 comparison over 400 passes (100 per shell, paired; the L and T60 schemes over 160). (a) SIB19 decodings per pass, mean with 95 % bootstrap interval over passes. (b) Share of served time with timing error above T_e'; shares below 0.01 % are not drawn.

Reference point Scheme Mean validity (s) SIB19 decodings per pass Passes above T_e' Largest error (ns) Satellite B0, fixed 5 s on a 2.56 s grid 5.0 109.1 0 153 Satellite B1, fixed 5 s on a 1 s grid 5.0 56.5 0 159 Satellite No expiry (V = 900 s), Kepler-J2 UE 900.0 1.0 0 207 Satellite Error-budget rule (--validity=budget) 612.9 1.6 0 162 Gateway T5, Taylor coefficients, 5 s 5.0 48.3 0 393 Gateway T-shell, Taylor, fixed table per shell 6.2 37.8 0 393 Gateway W-shell, window fit, fixed table per shell 17.5 14.1 0 294 Gateway Error-budget rule, window fit 25.1 10.4 0 370

What the data say: with the gateway as reference point, replacing Taylor coefficients by the window fit (--fit=window) cut decodings by a factor of 2.7 at the same validity table without a violation, and sizing the validity per epoch cut them by a further 1.35. Long validities with Taylor coefficients do fail: a fixed 60 s exceeded T_e' 76.4 % of the time. With the satellite as reference point no common term is broadcast, and a Kepler-J2 UE held one SIB19 for the whole pass. Values are copied from paper/tvt-2026-uplink-timing/make_macros.py, which sim/make_macros.py writes from sim/out_r4 and sim/out_r5.

docs.title: Architecture and classes
docs.text: Class / API Header Role NtnTimingAdvance model/ntn-timing-advance.h ComputeTotalTa() = 2(d_service + d_feeder)/c, ComputeCommonTa(), ComputeUeSpecificTa(), ComputeTaDriftRate(), ComputeTaDriftVariation(). The feeder leg is included for a transparent payload once a gateway mobility is set; a warning is logged when it is missing. EphemerisInfo, Sib19Content, Sib19Codec model/ntn-sib19.h NTN-Config-r17 content (ECEF state vector, ta-Common, drift and drift variation, ul-SyncValidityDuration, K_offset, kMac), fixed-layout serialization at the TS 38.331 field steps. NtnSib19Broadcaster model/ntn-sib19.h Periodic broadcaster driven by the live orbit. Uplink sync reference point (UlSyncReference: gateway or satellite), coefficient fit (Sib19CoefficientFit: Taylor, economized, window), validity rule (Sib19ValidityRule: slot over drift, error budget, fixed). Derives K_offset = ceil(RTT / slot) + 1. NtnUlTimingPrecompensator model/ntn-ul-timing-precompensator.h UE side: decodes SIB19, propagates the satellite (UeEphemerisModel: linear, gravity-ECEF, Kepler, Kepler-J2) from the last GNSS fix and forms TA(t) = 2|s(t) - p|/c + T_C + T_D tau + T_V tau^2. NtnRachWindow, NtnRachWindowVerdict model/ntn-rach-window.h The RAR window a given round trip demands and whether the configured ra-ResponseWindow can express it (TS 38.213 section 8.1, TR 38.821 section 7.3). NtnMeasReportCodec, NtnMeasQuantity model/ntn-meas-report.h MeasurementReport content quantized to TS 38.133 level indices (RSRP, RSRQ, SINR), saturating at the range ends. NtnDrxStateMachine, NtnDrxConfig model/ntn-drx.h Connected-mode DRX (Active, OnDuration, ShortSleep, LongSleep) plus an NTN AwaitingPass state between visibility windows. NtnUeLocationReporter model/ntn-ue-location-report.h Periodic, event-triggered and on-demand GNSS reports; closed-form ECEF and WGS-84 conversion. PayloadMode, TaReferenceFrame, GnssCapability model/ntn-rrc-types.h Transparent or regenerative payload, TA reference frame, UE GNSS capability. NtnRrcHelper helper/ntn-rrc-helper.h Installs timing advance, SIB19 broadcaster, location reporter and DRX on node pairs.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
./test.py -s ntn-rrc

The ntn-rrc suite (Type::UNIT, 28 test cases) covers closed-form TA for both payloads and the feeder leg, the common and UE-specific split, the LEO drift-rate bound, SIB19 codec round trip and truncation rejection, broadcaster cadence and K_offset, the UE pre-compensator, RACH window and measurement-report quantization, ECEF and WGS-84 round trips, the three location-report modes, and DRX including pass-aware sleep and invalid configurations.

docs.title: Scope and limitations
docs.text:
• SIB19 is serialized to a trace source and a buffer, and decoded by NtnUlTimingPrecompensator; it is not carried on BCCH or PDSCH of the radio stack.
  • K_offset is consumed only where NtnRealStackHelper::SetKOffsetConsumption() (in ntn-traffic) is enabled; the mmwave MAC never reads it.
  • The radio examples use the mmwave ideal RRC (UseIdealRrc=true): bearers are set up at attach with no over-the-air RRC PDU exchange, and the core is the LTE EPC, not a 5GC. The machinery here runs alongside that RRC as assistance and accounting.
  • The 0.64 s lead used in the Results section is in the study patch, not yet in this tree.

docs.title: ntn-sagin
docs.text:
title: ntn-sagin - Space-Air-Ground integrated network simulation for ns-3 description: Simulate SAGIN in ns-3: LEO satellites, HAPS, UAV swarms, aircraft and ground terminals over a 3GPP TR 36.777 air-to-ground channel and a real NR-NTN cell.

ntn-sagin

Space-air-ground integrated networking: ground, UAV, HAPS and LEO layers, a router that has to choose between them, and custody across contact gaps

Toolkit  |  Docs  |  Install  |  Examples  |  Results

Source

This page mirrors contrib/ntn-sagin/README.md. Figures are regenerated by the make_*.py scripts in contrib/ntn-sagin/doc/figures/.

docs.title: Why this module
docs.text:
A space-air-ground network gets interesting exactly where the layers disagree: a UAV relay that is close but short of capacity, a HAPS that is stable but rare, a LEO satellite that is fast but leaving. This module gives each layer real mobility and a real channel and makes the router pick from a pool of candidates rather than a fixed index. When no layer is in view, traffic can wait in custody instead of being dropped.

The air-to-ground channel is TR 36.777, and it keeps its own boundary: the recommendation is validated up to 300 m of aerial height, so calls above that are recorded and reportable rather than silently extrapolated. The chained excess-over-free-space loss is signed. Clamping it at zero sounds harmless, but it turns the model into plain Friis at short line-of-sight range and rectifies the shadow-fading distribution, which removed about 35 percent of draws at 1 km.

docs.title: System design
docs.text:
Figure 1. Classes of ntn-sagin. Mobility models of every layer feed the TR 36.777 channel, the layer routers and the custody queue each tick; the channel is chained onto a real NR NTN cell from ntn-traffic, and the router's hop path and the drained custody queue drive gated point-to-point IPv4 links. Source: ../media/ntn-sagin/make_architecture.py.

Class Header Role HapsMobilityModel, HapsTrajectoryMobilityModel haps-mobility-model.h, haps-trajectory-mobility-model.h Figure-8 (lemniscate) station keeping with a bounded vertical envelope; waypoint and loiter trajectory playback. UavWaypointMobilityModel, UavPatrolMobilityModel, UavSearchPatternMobilityModel uav-mobility-models.h Random waypoint, A to B patrol, lawnmower search. AeronauticalMobilityModel, OpenSkyMobilityModel aeronautical-scenario.h, opensky-mobility-model.h Constant-altitude cruise; aircraft replayed from OpenSky ADS-B traces. AisMobilityModel, HstMobilityModel ais-mobility-model.h, hst-mobility-model.h Vessels replayed from AIS records; high-speed train along a track. Trace loaders in ais-maritime-trace.h, hst-trace.h, opensky-adsb-trace.h, haps-trajectory-trace.h. A2gChannelTr36777 a2g-channel-tr36777.h TR 36.777 v15.0.0 path loss and LOS probability for UMa-AV, RMa-AV and UMi-AV. SaginA2gPropagationLossModel sagin-a2g-propagation-loss-model.h The same model as an ns-3 PropagationLossModel; chained onto a real NR spectrum channel it attenuates actual packets, returning the excess over free space to avoid double counting. MultiLayerRouter multi-layer-router.h Greedy max-elevation path computation over ground, UAV, HAPS and LEO candidates, with a pluggable score callback. Optional congestion awareness (SetLinkLoadSource, SetCongestionAware, default off): a filling link is penalized and one at the cutoff is rejected; a link of unknown load is scored on elevation, not assumed idle. Returns a SaginHop vector. SaginSliceRouter sagin-slice-router.h Wraps MultiLayerRouter: QFI to S-NSSAI to slice profile, layer choice biased by latency budget and a GEO allowance. SaginCustodyQueue sagin-custody-queue.h Store and forward: holds packets while the next hop is out of contact and drains them when it opens. FCFS by default, SetLastComeFirstServed, SetReplaceSameSource (keep only the newest per source), per-hop or end-to-end lifetime, byte capacity with oldest-first eviction. Counters: forwarded immediately, forwarded from custody, expired, dropped for space, largest custody delay. SaginHelper sagin-helper.h Builds a four-layer scene in one call.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
The results below come from a store-and-forward IoT study built on SaginCustodyQueue and examples/sagin-store-forward-iot.cc. Its code and data are in the toolkit workspace under paper/iotj-2026-store-and-forward/ (campaign driver run_ns3_sf4.py, outputs out/ns3_sf4.jsonl, 825 ns-3 runs from one binary; numbers by make_macros.py). Setup: the Orbcomm, Kinéis and Sateliot fleets, each satellite flying its own element set through Vallado SGP4; 60 ocean buoys and either five or eleven gateways; one 40-byte status update per buoy every 15 min; every (device, satellite) and (satellite, gateway) pair a 1 Mb/s point-to-point IPv4 link that drops all packets while the pair is out of view and whose delay follows the slant range; four simulated days, three with traffic; five replications with different buoy subsets and random-number runs. Radio access is not modeled.

Figure 2. ns-3, five replications, 95 % intervals. (a) Share of buoys that were ever served, bent pipe against store and forward to the first visible satellite and to the satellite with the earliest predicted delivery, per fleet and gateway set (5 or 11 sites). (b) Mean age of information on the buoys that bent pipe also serves, paired by buoy.

Fleet (5 gateways, ns-3, mean with 95 % half-width over 5 replications) Orbcomm Kinéis Sateliot Buoys served by bent pipe (%) 29 ± 3 25 ± 6 22 ± 6 Age of information on those buoys, bent pipe (h) 6.79 ± 1.97 1.26 ± 1.17 5.38 ± 0.24 Same buoys, store and forward (h) 1.76 ± 0.42 0.48 ± 0.04 4.57 ± 0.25 Updates delivered under keep-newest (%) 45.5 ± 1.2 59.1 ± 1.5 10.2 ± 0.7 Updates held on board, 99th percentile: FCFS / keep-newest 107 / 35 51 / 25 354 / 24 Storage cut, FCFS over keep-newest (per replication) 3.1 ± 0.2 2.1 ± 0.1 14.5 ± 0.9

Figure 3. Updates held by a satellite just before a gateway contact, 99th percentile over contacts, from the study's slot-level custody simulator on the same contact plans (mean over three weeks). (a) FCFS, keep-newest on the device only, keep-newest on device and board, and a bound computed from the previous week's plan. (b) The storage cut against the ratio of mean contact gap to update period.

In short: on every fleet, custody served all buoys where bent pipe reached 22 to 29 percent of them, and keeping only the newest update per device cut the on-board backlog by a factor of 2.1 to 14.5 while delivering a smaller share of updates. Figure 3 is from the study's own slot simulator, not from ns-3; the ns-3 table above is the packet-level check.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
Inside the toolkit, where the module is already present and built:

./ns3 run "sagin-store-forward-iot --policy=sf1 --days=2"
./ns3 run "ntn-sagin-remote-coverage --sharing=1"
./test.py -s ntn-sagin

Standalone, into an existing ns-3.43 tree:

git clone -b ntn-sagin-v2 https://github.com/Muhammaduazir69/ntn-sagin.git contrib/ntn-sagin
./ns3 configure --enable-examples --enable-tests
./ns3 build

INSTALL.md lists the dependencies. Most examples build on ntn-traffic (the real NR stack) and ntn-constellation (orbits), so the toolkit tree is the easiest place to run them.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Fourteen programs ship under examples/; binaries land at build/contrib/ntn-sagin/examples/ns3.43-<name>-default. Real-cell examples build an NR NTN cell with NtnRealStackHelper and print SINR, TBLER and throughput measured off the PHY trace, plus sim_health.csv in --outputDir. Data-plane examples build point-to-point IPv4 links with geometry-driven error models and measure delay, jitter, loss and goodput at NtnOranSink from the in-band header.

Example What it shows Command sagin-store-forward-iot Buoys report through a sparse LEO fleet (real element sets, Vallado SGP4) with custody on devices and satellites. --policy = bp (bent pipe), sf1 (store and forward to the highest satellite), sfe (earliest predicted delivery); --keepNewest, --lcfs, --lifetimeH. The server writes one line per received update. ./ns3 run "sagin-store-forward-iot --policy=sfe --keepNewest=1" ntn-sagin-remote-coverage Multi-operator sharing of one LEO cell for a remote village; with --sharing=1 the second operator's UEs ride the first operator's cell on their own S-NSSAI and the measured per-operator volume gives the cost split. ./ns3 run "ntn-sagin-remote-coverage --sharing=1" sagin-haps-leo-relay Ground UE to UAV relay to HAPS to LEO; the router logs per-hop elevation and range each second while the access hop is a real NR cell with the TR 36.777 channel. The route columns are a geometry trace and do not actuate traffic. ./ns3 run "sagin-haps-leo-relay --simTime=30 --csv=sagin.csv" sagin-uav-swarm Eight UAVs (waypoint, patrol, search) as UEs of a ground gNB over the RMa-AV channel; per-UAV SINR each second. ./ns3 run "sagin-uav-swarm --simTime=30 --fcGHz=2.0" sagin-a2g-real-stack SaginA2gPropagationLossModel chained onto a real NR air interface; the LOS and NLOS branches appear as a measured SINR and throughput gap. ./ns3 run "sagin-a2g-real-stack --duration=12 --link=NLOS --scenario=UMa_AV" sagin-aeronautical A cruise leg at 11 km and 250 m/s served by a passing LEO over a real NR cell; geometry logged, radio KPIs measured. ./ns3 run "sagin-aeronautical --simTime=30 --cruise=11000 --speed=250" sagin-flight-leo-e2 Long-haul flight with E2-KPM indications from the satellite gNB; a mid-pass elevation descent pushes measured SINR below threshold and logs a RELEASE event. ./ns3 run "sagin-flight-leo-e2 --simSeconds=30 --reportMs=500" sagin-multihop-traffic Three point-to-point hops, ground to UAV to HAPS to LEO, each with its own error model; the route is actuated, so it can be checked against per-leg bytes. ./ns3 run "sagin-multihop-traffic --simSeconds=60 --dataRateMbps=20" sagin-slice-traffic URLLC, eMBB and mMTC flows steered onto HAPS, LEO and GEO legs by latency budget; the mMTC flow on the GEO leg measures about 119 ms one-way, the 35 786 km propagation time. ./ns3 run "sagin-slice-traffic --simSeconds=60 --dataRateMbps=10" sagin-maritime-leo-traffic A vessel terminal under AisMobilityModel served by a passing LEO over a real NR cell. ./ns3 run "sagin-maritime-leo-traffic --simSeconds=30 --vesselSpeedKn=20" sagin-hst-leo-traffic A high-speed-train terminal served by a passing LEO over a real NR cell. ./ns3 run "sagin-hst-leo-traffic --simSeconds=30 --trainSpeedKmh=500" sagin-adsb-flight-leo-traffic An in-flight terminal replayed from an ADS-B trace, served by a passing LEO. ./ns3 run "sagin-adsb-flight-leo-traffic --simSeconds=30" sagin-sgp4-routed-traffic SGP4 shell plus contact-graph routing on a real IP data plane: contacts bring interfaces up and down, delays follow the slant range, global routing reroutes the live flow, cross-checked each second against the router's Dijkstra path. ./ns3 run "sagin-sgp4-routed-traffic --simSeconds=120 --altKm=550 --inclDeg=53" ntn-sagin-orphan-mobility-showcase A HAPS flying a loiter racetrack, a ground to HAPS to LEO packet plane, relay geometry and Doppler from live positions, optional NetSimulyzer JSON and Cesium CZML. ./ns3 run "ntn-sagin-orphan-mobility-showcase --duration=120"

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
./test.py -s ntn-sagin

test/ntn-sagin-test-suite.cc registers 42 test cases: HAPS, UAV, aeronautical, OpenSky, AIS and HST mobility (importers, interpolation, replay under simulator time), the TR 36.777 path loss, LOS probability, fading, validated height band and signed excess loss, the multi-layer router (scorers, congestion awareness, gating a data plane), slice routing, and the custody queue (forwarding, expiry, LCFS, end-to-end lifetime).

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text:
• ns-3.43: core, network, internet, mobility, propagation, point-to-point, applications; toolkit module ntn-slice (linked by CMakeLists.txt).
  • Examples: ntn-traffic (NtnRealStackHelper, NtnOranApplication), ntn-constellation (orbits, contact graph), and the toolkit's mmwave.
  • Sample data in data/: AIS and OpenSky traces, buoy and gateway sites, Orbcomm, Kinéis and Sateliot element sets.

docs.title: Scope and limitations
docs.text:
• Custody, not DTN. SaginCustodyQueue holds and drains packets. There is no RFC 5050 bundle format, no custody signaling and no fragmentation.
  • Routers compute paths. MultiLayerRouter and SaginSliceRouter return hop vectors and install no forwarding table. In sagin-haps-leo-relay and sagin-aeronautical the route is a geometry trace that no measured KPI validates; sagin-multihop-traffic is the example where the route is actuated.
  • Regenerative payload. RegenMode in ntn-constellation filters Dijkstra transit and decides whether a satellite may run an Xn handover (NtnXnHandover: HANDOVER REQUEST, ACKNOWLEDGE, SN STATUS TRANSFER, UE CONTEXT RELEASE over the ISL, 20.01 ms at 1500 km measured). The XnAP messages are an ns-3 Header with toolkit-internal type values, not ASN.1 APER, and the Xn path is not yet wired to the NrGnbNetDevice that NtnRealStackHelper can build on a satellite. In sagin-sgp4-routed-traffic the satellites are plain IP routers. Treat ISL paths as transparent unless you wire that yourself.
  • A2G validity. TR 36.777 is validated to 300 m aerial height; calls above it are recorded, not hidden.
