docs.title: ntn-sionna
docs.text:
GPU ray tracing for the last kilometer of an NTN link: NVIDIA Sionna RT bridged into ns-3, with provenance on every query

Toolkit  ·  Docs  ·  Install  ·  Examples  ·  Results

docs.title: Why this module
docs.text:
A closed-form NTN channel such as TR 38.811 is fast and reproducible, but it folds every building into one shadowing term and one LOS-probability table. For a street-level user that is the part that decides whether the link exists. ntn-sionna lets ns-3 ask a ray tracer instead: an opt-in PropagationLossModel streams {tx, rx, freq_hz} to a Sionna RT server that keeps the scene resident on a GPU, over a socket, so the GPU need not be on the machine running the simulation.

The part worth stressing is honesty about when tracing did not happen. A missing server used to degrade silently to free space. Now traced and fallback evaluations are counted separately, every run reports which path produced its numbers, and SetRequireLiveTransport(true) makes a missing server fatal where a traced result is load-bearing. Caching and replay transports let a whole simulation run with no GPU at all, and a calibrator compares traced loss against the TR 38.811 reference under its own declared configuration.

docs.title: System design
docs.text: Figure 1. Classes and data flow. The ns-3 side (C++, bridge/) sends queries through a pluggable transport; sionna-server.py answers from a scene held on the GPU. The cascade model adds the ITU-R atmosphere that Sionna RT does not model; the CIR model applies caller-supplied taps with per-tap Doppler. A stub server with the same wire protocol serves the tests. Source: doc/figures/make_architecture.py.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
The results below are a ray-tracing study of street-level LEO links in four city scenes. They were computed with Sionna RT 2.0.1 directly from Python, the solver this bridge serves, by the study scripts in paper/tvt-2026-urban-los/ of the toolkit tree (sky_maps2.py for the sky maps, analysis2.py, analysis3.py and loss_summary.py for the statistics; commands in sim/README_runs.md). They did not pass through the ns-3 bridge; they show what the traced channel says that the closed-form default does not.

Experiment. The Munich, Paris, Florence and San Francisco scenes shipped with Sionna RT; 300 outdoor users per city at 1.5 m, two independent user realizations; 2 GHz, isotropic antennas; LOS, reflection and edge diffraction to depth 3 with 10^9 rays per user; a direction grid from 15 to 85 degrees elevation and 0 to 355 degrees azimuth in 5 degree steps. Intervals are 95 % cluster-bootstrap intervals over users. Every number is ray traced, none is a field measurement.

Figure 2. LOS probability against elevation for street-level users: ray traced (markers, 95 % cluster-bootstrap band), a first-facade model built from the same city (solid), an idealized canyon (dash-dot), the S-band fit of Schreiber et al. at 1.5 m (dotted) and the TR 38.811 tables (crosses).

City LOS probability at 30 degrees (ray traced) Florence (compact medieval center) 26 % Munich (old town, squares, avenues) 36 % San Francisco (hilly mid-rise grid) 49 % Paris (Etoile, radiating avenues) 71 %

Of the two TR 38.811 tables, the better one per city had a mean error of 4 to 11 percentage points and a largest error of 7 to 21 points against the traced curve. A second user realization moved the mean LOS at 30 degrees by at most 3 points.

Figure 3. Excess loss of blocked directions against elevation, smooth 0.3 m concrete facades: censored median per city with 10th to 90th percentile band, against the TR 38.811 clutter loss for NLOS at S band, the Schreiber et al. fit and the ITU-R P.681 Annex 2 bad-state total measured at 2.2 GHz.

Censored median excess loss, blocked directions, 0.3 m concrete (dB) 15 to 30 deg 30 to 60 deg 60 to 85 deg Munich 21.2 20.5 28.9 Paris 18.6 22.3 21.3 Florence 26.0 19.5 19.7 San Francisco 19.9 21.2 19.9 TR 38.811 clutter loss (reference) 31.1 27.6 25.8

Below 60 degrees every city lay under the TR 38.811 clutter value, by 3 to 13 dB with smooth concrete over both realizations (intervals about plus or minus 3 dB), 6 to 14 dB with the shipped marble and 11 to 15 dB with rough concrete. Medians are censored: directions no ray reached (1 to 12 % with smooth concrete) count as above any finite value, so they lean high. Above 60 degrees the sign is unsettled. Values are copied from paper/tvt-2026-urban-los/make_macros2.py, written by sim/make_macros2.py.

Module-level check you can run. The bridge's own calibration path is sionna-calibration-harness, which drives SionnaCalibrator against the TR 38.811 reference and reports the residual with its gate. No stored output of a live-server run is kept in the tree, so run it against your server:

python3 contrib/ntn-sionna/bridge/sionna-server.py --port 8765 &
./ns3 run "sionna-calibration-harness --host=127.0.0.1 --port=8765"

docs.title: Architecture and classes
docs.text:
Class Header (bridge/) Role NtnSionnaChannel ns3-sionna-channel.h Opt-in PropagationLossModel; FSPL fallback on timeout, counted and optionally fatal (SetRequireLiveTransport) SionnaTransport, SionnaNoneTransport sionna-transport.h Transport contract; request carries optional array and RIS configuration and los_only SionnaUdpTransport sionna-udp-transport.h UDP client of a live sionna-server.py SionnaPybindTransport sionna-pybind-transport.h In-process transport (built with ENABLE_SIONNA_PYBIND11) SionnaCachingTransport sionna-caching-transport.h 4-D LRU decorator; array, RIS and los_only are part of the key SionnaReplayTransport (SionnaReplayWriter, SionnaReplayReader) sionna-replay-transport.h Record once, replay without a GPU SionnaBatchClient sionna-batch-client.h Synchronous and asynchronous batched queries NtnSionnaCascadeChannel ntn-sionna-cascade-channel.h Traced loss plus NtnAtmosphericLossChain NtnAtmosphericLossChain (Itu618, Itu676, Itu681) ntn-atmospheric-loss-chain.h Gaseous, rain and LMS shadowing chain NtnAtmosphericPropagationLossModel ntn-atmospheric-propagation-loss-model.h ITU-R excess only, chainable on any spectrum channel without double-counting FSPL SionnaCirPropagationLossModel sionna-cir-propagation-loss-model.h Multipath CIR with per-tap Doppler from the endpoints' live velocity; taps are supplied by the caller CirDopplerSynthesizer cir-doppler-synth.h Advances a CIR snapshot by Doppler rotation SionnaCalibrator sionna-calibrator.h Residual of traced loss against a reference model, with a declared LOS mode and reach

Python side: bridge/sionna-server.py (scene loaded once, JSON over UDP, default port 8765, LOS-only or full multipath), tools/ (osm_to_sionna_scene.py, lidar_dem_ingest.py, probe_sionna_env.py), test/sionna-stub-server.py (same protocol, closed-form FSPL).

./ns3 run "leo-pass-sionna-vs-tr38811 --sionnaServer=127.0.0.1:8765"

docs.text:

pytest contrib/ntn-sionna/test/          # Python server tests

docs.text:

docs.title: ntn-slice
docs.text:
Network slicing on a satellite cell in ns-3: per-slot RBG quotas enforced in the NR MAC, controllers that follow the pass, and SLA monitors that report tails rather than means

Toolkit  ·  Docs  ·  Install  ·  Examples  ·  Results

docs.title: Why this module
docs.text:
A slice is only a slice if the radio treats it differently. On a LEO cell that is harder than on the ground, because what a resource block carries changes over a pass: as the satellite recedes, the slant range grows, the MCS drops and a share that was enough at the start of the pass stops being enough near its end.

ntn-slice provides both halves. NtnSliceQuotaScheduler, a 5G-LENA OFDMA proportional-fair scheduler, enforces a per-slot RBG quota for each slice and lends what a slice leaves unused, so the partition is real in the MAC. The examples close loops around it: quotas from the ephemeris, from measured backlog and bytes per RBG, or from a tenant's rate contract with a delivered-rate trim. Around this sit the slice vocabulary (S-NSSAI, SliceProfile with TS 22.261 defaults, a flow selector), a GEO mode-skip rule for latency-bound slices, and an isolation monitor that keeps a delay histogram, so a p99 is a percentile and not a mean.

docs.title: System design
docs.text: Figure 1. Classes and data flow. The selector maps flows (and through RNTIs, UEs) to slices; controllers in the examples call SetQuotas() on NtnSliceQuotaScheduler every control period and read back its measured counters. SliceOrchestratorXapp is a shadow allocator: its PRB split is logged but does not reach the MAC. Source: doc/figures/make_architecture.py.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
The results come from a slicing study on a LEO pass, run with this module's ntn-slice-pass-leo and ntn-slice-tenants-leo examples on a 5G-LENA cell. The study binaries are those examples with passive additions not yet merged here (block counters read from the UE PHY trace, a queue-proportional baseline, an --aLimited switch); no scheduler code differs. Patch, regression check and campaign scripts: paper/tnsm-2026-slice-quotas/ of the toolkit tree (ns3_patch/, compare_rev.py, run_final.py, make_macros5.py).

Experiment. One cell of 2.185 GHz and 20 MHz (numerology 1) through a 550 km, 53 degree SGP4 satellite with 55 dBm and an 8 x 8 array, free space plus TR 38.811 excess loss. The UE cluster sees the satellite recede from 87 to 31 degrees elevation over a 120 s run. Each mechanism runs on the same 12 seeds; every number below is a median over those seeds.

Figure 2. Delay-critical slice (16 Mb/s, 50 ms budget) at full load over the falling pass: 99th-percentile one-way delay (left) and share of packets over 50 ms (right) per 5 s window, medians over 12 seeds. Thin lines mark 50 ms and 1 %; a share of zero is drawn at 0.01 %.

Mechanism (--policy) p99 delay, median (worst seed) p99.9 delay Windows over target (%) eMBB (Mb/s) All (Mb/s) PF, no slices (pf) 2.8 s (6.7 s) 3.4 s 91 18.6 34.5 Two equal BWPs (bwp) 133 ms (429 ms) 261 ms 26 20.6 36.6 Static quota sized at the start (static) 2.6 s (3.6 s) 3.4 s 52 15.2 31.1 Static quota sized at the end (static) 16 ms (22 ms) 39 ms 0 14.8 30.9 Ephemeris-driven quota (predict) 20 ms (33 ms) 49 ms 0 14.2 30.3 Measured closed loop (reactive) 19 ms (26 ms) 47 ms 0 14.4 30.4 5QI priority, 5QI 79 (qos) 15 ms (54 ms) 58 ms 0 17.2 33.3 5QI priority, 5QI 3 (qos) 14 ms (15 ms) 32 ms 0 17.1 33.2

What the data say: on the calibration seed the delay-critical slice carried 77 bytes per RBG at 87 degrees and 50 at 31 degrees, 36 % less, so the quota it needs rises from 0.48 to 0.74 of the RBGs. A quota sized for the start of the pass failed once that headroom was used up; the measured loop and the ephemeris loop both kept up, and knowing the orbit bought nothing measurable over measuring. Priority with the strong 5QI 3 class gave the lowest tail, and both priority settings left eMBB about 2.7 Mb/s more than the measured loop; the study traces most of that lead to how this stack schedules retransmissions, not to the priority rule itself.

Figure 3. Two tenants on the same cell, contract R = 12 Mb/s for tenant A, decoding errors on, medians over 12 seeds. Tenant B pauses in the shaded interval. "Queue-proportional" is the study-only baseline.

Mechanism (--policy) A (Mb/s) Lowest A window Busy windows below R B (Mb/s) Busy total (Mb/s) PF, no slices (pf) 17.6 15.4 0 % 17.4 35.0 5QI priority (qos) 25.1 20.6 0 % 8.1 33.3 Rate cap, no lending (policed) 12.0 12.0 0 % 27.4 39.4 Rate cap, lending (limiter) 12.0 12.0 0 % 27.5 39.5 Static quota, start of pass (static) 12.5 10.6 33 % 19.9 32.5 Static quota, best of sweep, 0.42 (static) 15.2 12.4 0 % 17.3 32.5 Contract quota (contract) 14.3 13.4 0 % 18.3 32.6 Contract quota, ephemeris table (contract_eph) 14.4 12.9 0 % 18.1 32.4 Trimmed contract loop (contract_trim) 12.6 12.5 0 % 19.8 32.5

The trimmed loop held tenant A near its 12.6 Mb/s target and left tenant B more than the best fixed quota did; the rate cap with lending left B the most, and the cap without lending held A at 12.0 Mb/s even while B was idle, so it is not work conserving. Values are copied from paper/tnsm-2026-slice-quotas/make_macros5.py, written by sim/make_macros5.py from the run outputs in sim/out/.

docs.title: Architecture and classes
docs.text:
Header Provides model/ntn-slice-quota-scheduler.h NtnSliceQuotaScheduler (derived from NrMacSchedulerOfdmaPF): SetSliceOfRnti(), SetQuotas(), TakeRbgCounts(), TakeBacklog(), TakeBytesPerRbg(), and a per-slot allocation trace. A slice with demand gets at least floor(quota x RBGs) per slot; leftover RBGs go to any slice with data. Uplink stays plain PF. model/ntn-slice-contract-trim.h TrimmedQuota(): scales a tenant quota by (target bytes / delivered bytes)^gain, clamped. model/ntn-slice-types.h SliceSst, Snssai (8-bit SST + 24-bit SD, packed codecs), SliceProfile, default eMBB, URLLC and mMTC profiles after TS 22.261 Table 7.1-1. model/ntn-slice-selector.h NtnSliceSelector: DSCP, port-range and app-label rule chain, first match wins, default fallback. model/slice-orchestrator-xapp.h SliceOrchestratorXapp: min-throughput reservation plus priority-weighted sharing; Step() and StepWithShares() for an RL policy. Shadow allocator, see limitations. model/slice-isolation-monitor.h SliceIsolationMonitor: rolling per-slice p99 delay and cumulative loss, BreachEvent records. helper/ntn-slice-helper.h NtnSliceHelper::ThreeSliceDefault(), ShouldSkipGeo(), IsGeoSatellite() (30 000 km boundary).

A Grafana dashboard (dashboards/ntn-slice.json) plugs into the stack of the ntn-observability module.

docs.title: Scope and limitations
docs.text:
• The quota scheduler acts on the downlink only; the uplink is scheduled by the parent PF scheduler unchanged.
  • SliceOrchestratorXapp is an open-loop shadow allocator: its PRB decisions are computed and logged but do not drive any MAC. In the three mmwave examples the 5QI and S-NSSAI are packet labels the MAC never reads, and isolation there is observed, not enforced. Enforcement is the 5G-LENA quota scheduler path.
  • The V2X SST value (4) is defined but has no default profile.
  • The Results are one cell, one satellite pass geometry and 12 seeds; the queue-proportional baseline and the block counters exist only in the study patch.

docs.title: ntn-traffic - the real 5G NR NTN data plane under satellite mobility in ns-3
docs.text:
ntn-traffic

The real-stack spine: a 5G NR NTN data plane under satellite mobility, with every KPI measured in band

Toolkit  |  Docs  |  Install  |  Examples  |  Results

Source

This page mirrors contrib/ntn-traffic/README.md. Figures are regenerated by the make_*.py scripts in contrib/ntn-traffic/doc/figures/.

docs.title: Why this module
docs.text:
Most satellite network studies compute their KPIs from a closed form: slant range over the speed of light for latency, a Shannon bound for throughput, a threshold for loss. That is fast, and it makes the mechanism under study impossible to falsify, because the KPI cannot disagree with the model that produced it. ntn-traffic exists so that it can disagree.

NtnRealStackHelper assembles a genuine NR cell, either the mmWave backend or 5G-LENA nr at FR1, and puts it under satellite mobility: a real SpectrumPhy, an LDPC error model, RLC and PDCP with timers relaxed to the slant round trip, RRC, and an EPC with GTP tunneling. Delay, jitter and loss then come from an in-band header that carries a sequence number and a transmit timestamp through the tunnel, so they are properties of packets that crossed the air interface. Every scenario writes a health record that labels each KPI as measured, modeled or configured, so a reader can tell the difference without reading the code. This module is the spine the other toolkit modules build their examples on, which is why it ships only inside the toolkit tree.

docs.title: System design
docs.text: Figure 1. The caller supplies satellite and ground nodes that already carry mobility, plus any module physics; NtnRealStackHelper builds the NR NTN cell and chains the NTN channel models onto it. ORAN applications carry their QoS identity and timestamps in band through GTP, and NtnOranAiFlowMonitor turns the flows into KPM series for oran-ntn, ns3-ai-ntn and the exporters. Source: ../media/ntn-traffic/make_architecture.py.

docs.title: Real-radio helper (helper/ntn-real-stack-helper.h)
docs.text: Area API Notes Build Build(gnbNodes, ueNodes), SetRadioBackend, SetCarrierFrequencyHz, SetBandwidthHz, SetSatEirpDbm, SetUeTxPowerDbm Both node sets must already carry a MobilityModel (SGP4, TR 38.811, HAPS). Default carrier 2 GHz. Payload SetPayloadOption, SetFeederGeometry, ComputePayloadExtraDelay Transparent (2 x slant/c), RegenerativeRu (slant/c + 0.25 ms), RegenerativeRuDu (slant/c + 0.15 ms), FullGnb (slant/c + 0.05 ms, default); feeder delay re-evaluated every second from live geometry. HARQ and RLC SetHarqEnabled, SetNtnHarqProfile, SetRlcAmEnabled HARQ is off by default because terrestrial timers break over the slant; the NTN profile rescales the HARQ timeout and process count from the geometry. Shipped runs carry RLC UM. Uplink timing SetKOffsetConsumption, ComputeKOffsetSlots, GetGnbN2Delay Opt-in, nr backend: K_offset = ceil(RTT / slot) + 1, programmed into the UL DCI to PUSCH gap (TS 38.213 Section 4.2). Uses a vendored nr patch that raises the N2Delay cap. Channel AddExtraPropagationLoss, AddSpectrumChannelLoss, SetChannelUpdatePeriod, SetTddPattern Chains module physics (THz, Sionna RT, A2G) onto the live channel; the 3GPP channel regenerates every 100 ms so clusters follow the satellite. Traffic InstallTraffic(profile, start, stop), InstallOranFlow(ueIdx, fiveQi, sst, sd, profile, start, stop) Canned mixes backed by NtnOranApplication. Measurement EnableAiFlowMonitor(prefix), Collect(), GetMeanDlSinrDb, GetMeanDlTbler, GetRxThroughputMbps, GetMeanDelayMs, GetUeRecentSinrDb, WriteHealthReport() sim_health.csv gates assert trace provenance (transport blocks decoded, SINR from the PHY trace, an active error model); its air_interface tag is derived from the carrier per TS 38.104.

docs.title: ORAN application suite and flow monitor (model/)
docs.text:
Class Role NtnOranPayloadHeader 24-byte in-band header: version, payload type, per-flow sequence (u32), TX timestamp in ns (u64), 5QI, S-NSSAI SST and SD, QFI, source and destination IDs. Rides inside the GTP tunnel, so it survives re-encapsulation. NtnOranApplication Traffic source with TS 23.501 profiles: conversational voice (5QI 1), eMBB video (5QI 2), URLLC periodic (5QI 82), mMTC periodic, Poisson background (5QI 9), saturating CBR. NtnOranSink Per QoS flow: one-way delay from the in-band timestamp, RFC 3550 jitter, loss from sequence gaps, throughput over the active span. NtnCommandAndControlApp Platform telemetry (5QI 69) sampled from the node's real mobility, with a battery model. NtnOranAiFlowMonitor, NtnOranFlowClassifier, NtnOranFlowProbe Built on ns-3 FlowMonitor; flows keyed by QoS identity instead of the IP 5-tuple; KPM series under TS 28.552 names (DRB.UEThpDl, DRB.RlcSduDelayDl, DRB.PacketLossRateDl, L1M.RS-SINR, ...); sliding-window features; EWMA z-score anomalies; XML, CSV, InfluxDB line protocol and E2SM-KPM-shaped exporters. NtnTr38811ExcessLossModel, NtnSatBeamGainModel, NtnSpectrumSeamModel, NtnTdlSpectrumPropagationLossModel, NtnStaticExtraLossModel TR 38.811 excess loss with the scenario shadow-fading tables; the TR 38.811 Section 6.4.1 circular-aperture (Airy) beam pattern; a spectrum seam that composes losses; a frequency-selective tapped delay line (stand-in tap table); a runtime scalar loss for blockage or RIS events.

The module also keeps the classic generators: 3GPP HTTP over a satellite link, NRTV video over TCP or UDP, a CBR application, and the lightweight NtnRealisticTrafficHelper point-to-point data plane (no radio physics).

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
Measured radio against the 3GPP TR 38.821 Section 6.1.3 link-budget method, from a ten-seed campaign of the two shipped calibration examples (stored in the toolkit workspace under papers/paper1_ojcoms_toolkit/revision_experiments/r1_seeds/: per-seed run folders, r1_calibration_samples.csv, r1_arraygain_samples.csv and the summaries, September 2026). Study case Set-1 LEO-600, S-band downlink, handheld terminal, mmwave backend, a real SGP4 satellite at 600 km. Commands: ntn-tr38821-calibration --simSeconds=600 --radio=mmwave --RngRun=1..10, and ntn-tr38821-array-gain-calibration with --boresightMode=point and nadir, RngRun 1 to 10. The figure is built by ../media/ntn-traffic/make_results.py.

Figure 2. (a) SINR measured off the PHY trace against the TR 38.821 closed-form CNR over the pass, elevation at or above 10 deg, 10 seeds x 132 samples; the dashed line is the closed form shifted by the mean measured offset. (b) Beam pattern recovered from the paired difference of a fixed-boresight and a steered run sampled at the same instants, against the analytic TR 38.811 Airy pattern, 10 seeds x 118 pairs.

Measured (10 seeds, mean with 95 % Student-t half-width across seeds) Value Offset of measured SINR over the TR closed form, elevation at or above 10 deg 4.06 ± 0.22 dB Within-run spread of that offset (standard deviation) 2.47 dB SINR decay from zenith to 10 deg: measured / TR free-space prediction 10.47 ± 1.30 dB / 9.97 dB Beam pattern, fixed ground point: angles swept / RMS error / bias 1.90 to 5.73 deg (0.87 beamwidths) / 2.85 ± 0.24 dB / 0.32 ± 0.58 dB Beam pattern, nadir-fixed: angles swept / RMS error 1.27 to 50.5 deg / 2.71 ± 0.21 dB

Reading this honestly: the measured decay follows the TR free-space prediction within its interval, and the constant offset is the array gain of the spectrum model, reported rather than calibrated away. The examples' own pass or fail gates are stricter than the aggregate. On these 600 s runs the calibration example printed FAIL every time, because its spread gate is evaluated over all samples, including geometry below the horizon. The array-gain example's pattern gate (RMS under 3 dB) passed in all ten nadir runs and in five of the ten fixed-ground-point runs.

docs.text:

NtnRealStackHelper rs;
rs.SetSimTime(Seconds(30));
rs.SetOutputDir("out");
rs.Build(satNodes, ueNodes);                  // nodes already carry mobility
rs.InstallOranFlow(0, 82, 2, 0x000001, NtnOranApplication::URLLC_PERIODIC, Seconds(1), Seconds(29));
rs.EnableAiFlowMonitor("my-run");
Simulator::Stop(Seconds(30));
Simulator::Run();
rs.Collect();
rs.WriteHealthReport();
Simulator::Destroy();

docs.title: Scope and limitations
docs.text:
• mmwave backend numerology. On the mmwave path the S-band carrier runs with FR2 numerology (60 kHz SCS) on a terrestrial 8 x 8 array gNB, with the satellite EIRP applied as a conducted transmit power; it is not a reflector beam with a 3 dB footprint. Use SetRadioBackend for 5G-LENA at FR1.
  • HARQ off, RLC UM by default. Turn them on deliberately; the defaults reflect what the terrestrial timers tolerate over the slant.
  • Multi-UE uplink. K_offset consumption enables single-UE or downlink-heavy uplink under a real air-interface delay; full multi-UE uplink also needs per-UE timing advance and NTN-aware SRS and PUCCH timing, which the vendored nr v3.3 lacks.
  • TDL tap table. NtnTdlSpectrumPropagationLossModel uses a documented stand-in, not TR 38.811 Table 6.9.2, so "NTN-TDL" is not claimable.
  • Multi-UE NR handover. ntn-nr-handover-pass with more than one UE hits a limitation of the vendored 5G-LENA X2 data-forwarding path; the A3 and X2 decision itself fires.
  • Half-duplex collisions are dropped and counted (halfduplex_*_drops in sim_health.csv) rather than fatal; read them next to phy_rx_tb.

title: ntn-v2x - V2X over LEO satellites with SUMO mobility in ns-3 description: Simulate NTN-assisted V2X in ns-3: SUMO-driven vehicles choosing direct or satellite-relay links on the measured SINR of a real mmwave NR LEO cell.

ntn-v2x

Satellite-assisted V2X: NR sidelink Mode 2, SAE J2735 basic safety messages, and relay decisions that gate real packets

Toolkit  |  Docs  |  Install  |  Examples  |  Results

Source

This page mirrors contrib/ntn-v2x/README.md. Figures are regenerated by the make_*.py scripts in contrib/ntn-v2x/doc/figures/.

docs.title: Why this module
docs.text:
Vehicles that leave terrestrial coverage are the obvious NTN use case, and an easy one to fake: packet reception ratio against distance can be produced by a threshold without a single packet. Here the sidelink carries real messages. Basic safety messages are encoded the way SAE J2735 encodes them, a 21-octet core with UPER offset-from-lower-bound integers and the standard's range clamps. That matters more than it sounds: DE_Elevation spans -4096 to 61439, wider than a signed 16-bit integer, so a naive cast turns a legal 6000 m altitude into -553.6 m.

Relay decisions actuate. A runtime transmit gate lets a decision start and stop a flow mid-run, which ns-3 application start and stop times cannot, so a direct-versus-relay policy shows up as real traffic from terminals on air against exactly zero from gated ones. Re-measured on 2026-09-01 on the default run: 14 792 packets on air, 0 gated (an earlier count of 28 892 stopped reproducing when the spine's default carrier and width moved to 2.185 GHz and 20 MHz; the zero is what the claim rests on). Vehicles are real UEs carrying their own PHY measurements, so blockage varies per vehicle rather than by loop parity.

docs.title: System design
docs.text:
Figure 1. Classes of ntn-v2x. Vehicle traces drive SumoTraciBridge; each vehicle broadcasts a J2735 BSM over the NR Mode-2 sidelink; decoded announcements feed the relay decision, which gates the vehicle's uplink to SGP4 satellites (an NR NTN cell or a point-to-point path whose delay follows the slant range). V2xLeoDirect is kept only as a closed-form reference. Source: ../media/ntn-v2x/make_architecture.py.

Header Provides model/sumo-traci-bridge.h SumoTraciBridge: offline replay of floating-car data (LoadFcdTrace(csv), columns time,vehid,x,y,z,speed). Applies position and velocity, so GetVelocity() and the BSM speed and heading fields are real; register a ConstantVelocityMobilityModel, since a constant-position model cannot hold a velocity (dropped samples are counted by VelocitySamplesDropped()). Tracks sync jitter and exports per-vehicle samples through a TracedCallback. model/ntn-nr-sidelink.h NR PC5 sidelink Mode 2 (TS 38.321 Section 5.22). NtnSlResourcePool (subchannels x slots, TS 38.331 SL-ResourcePool); NtnSlUeMac (sensing-based autonomous selection: candidates in the T1..T2 window, exclusion above an SL-RSRP threshold, the 20 percent rule with 3 dB steps, periodic reservation with a reselection counter); NtnSlChannel (TR 37.885 highway LOS path loss with log-normal shadowing and NLOSv blockage, half duplex, SINR decode against thermal noise plus noise figure with co-channel interference summed in linear power, TS 38.885 PRR through GetPrr and GetPrrWithinRange). model/ntn-v2x-bsm-header.h NtnV2xBsmHeader: SAE J2735 (2016) BSMcoreData as an ns-3 Header, 21 octets on the wire (1 + 4 + 2 + 4 + 4 + 2 + 2 + 2), fields in J2735 resolutions; SetFromState() fills it from SI quantities. model/v2x-leo-relay.h V2xLeoRelay: per-vehicle direct or relay assignment with m_minDirectSnrDb and m_maxV2vRangeM; EvaluateAll() returns the decisions. model/v2x-leo-direct.h V2xLeoDirect: closed-form vehicle to LEO budget (free-space loss, SNR, elevation), kept as a comparison baseline; the examples decide on measured SINR. model/maritime-scenario.h MaritimeMobilityModel: deprecated, offline tests only. The maritime path is ntn-v2x-maritime-ais, which replays recorded AIS tracks through ntn-sagin. helper/ntn-v2x-helper.h WriteDeterministicTestFcdCsv: a disclosed, RNG-free FCD trace for the test suite.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
The figures and numbers below come from a street-canyon relaying study built on examples/ntn-v2x-canyon-relay.cc and this module's Mode-2 sidelink (paper/tits-2026-sidelink-relay/: code and data; main campaign run_ns3_canyon5.py, outputs out/ns3_canyon5.jsonl, numbers by make_macros5.py). Setup: the 638 Starlink satellites that CelesTrak labels direct-to-cell (43 and 53 deg inclination, near 350 km), propagated with SGP4 from element sets of 2 October 2026; a straight street in Manhattan whose facade heights are drawn once per run; line of sight to each satellite decided every 100 ms by the exact ray geometry against the facades; SUMO stop-and-go traffic on a 1.2 km ring (two lanes per direction, a signal every 240 m); one status report per vehicle per second; an assumed shared uplink of 300 kb/s per satellite. Each rule ran at 20 start times per canyon (10 in the suburban case), each start with its own facade draw, signal offsets, vehicle placement and satellite pass.

Figure 2. Mean age of information at the server, analytical model against ns-3, one marker per start, for eight baseline forwarding rules in the urban and the dense canyon. The model takes the facade-height law, the geometry, the SUMO trajectories and each run's measured mean delay.

Figure 3. Left: excess-age ratio of a fresh relay draw to a kept relay against the message period over the passage time, analysis, Monte Carlo and ns-3. Right: age as a median paired ratio to the nearest announcing neighbor at the same uplink budget against the uplink capacity per satellite, ten second-half starts (solid urban, dashed dense).

Measured in ns-3 (median over 20 starts) Urban canyon Dense canyon Age of information, serving satellite only 4.08 s 8.42 s Age of information, any satellite in line of sight 1.19 s 3.63 s Age of information, nearest neighbor that announced an uplink 0.53 s 0.58 s Distance driven since the server's newest report: any satellite / nearest announcer 7.8 m / 3.3 m 24.3 m / 3.6 m Uplink forwards per blocked message, two random announcers 1.9 1.8 Uplink forwards per blocked message, thinned every-decoder forwarding 4.9 4.5 Model error on the age above its floor, eight baseline rules (median) 23 % 20 %

The one-bit uplink announcement carried in each broadcast is what makes a single named relay work. Among forwarding rules the differences were smaller and lay mostly in uplink cost. Forwarding is at the application layer, and visibility rests on building geometry rather than a measured satellite channel.

docs.text:

  • Examples: ntn-traffic (NtnRealStackHelper, NtnOranApplication), ntn-constellation (SGP4), ntn-cho (TR 38.811 terminals), ntn-sagin (AIS replay), oran-ntn (xApp in the URLLC example), the toolkit's mmwave.

docs.title: Scope and limitations
docs.text:
• Offline replay only. ConnectTcp() opens a socket and closes it; the TraCI stepping protocol is not implemented, so live SUMO co-simulation is not available. Convert SUMO fcd-export to the CSV dialect.
  • MAC abstraction. The sidelink models resource pools, sensing, reservation, half duplex, collisions and an SINR decode. It does not decode PSCCH/PSSCH bits, combine HARQ or model second-stage SCI formats.
  • Read PRR against distance with care. At 23 dBm and 5.9 GHz the TR 37.885 highway model closes a link to roughly 9.6 km, about twenty times the platoon's span, so the shipped highway scenario is not range limited. Measured PRR within 50 m was 1.000 at 10 vehicles and 0.997 at 30 and at 60; the residual loss comes from half duplex and same-subchannel collisions. A curve that falls off within a few hundred meters needs TR 37.885 densities and offered load.
  • The shipped FCD traces are synthetic fixtures, not SUMO microsimulations; the canyon study used SUMO 1.18 traces generated by its own make_traces.py.

docs.title: oran-ntn - O-RAN Near-RT RIC and E2 for Satellite NTN
docs.text:
oran-ntn

Space O-RAN for ns-3: E2 and A1 control loops over a measured NR NTN radio, with the RIC placed on board, at a gateway or in the cloud

Toolkit  ·  Docs  ·  Install  ·  Results  ·  Examples

Source

This page mirrors contrib/oran-ntn/README.md. Figures are regenerated by the make_*.py scripts in contrib/oran-ntn/doc/figures/.

docs.title: Why this module
docs.text: Putting a RAN Intelligent Controller (RIC) in space is an architecture question before it is an algorithm question. Where the RIC sits decides how stale its view is when a decision lands, and whether the satellite can still act when its feeder link to the ground is down. oran-ntn makes those questions measurable in ns-3. The RIC placement is an experiment variable whose E2 latency comes from live slant geometry, the KPIs the xApps read are measured on a real NR NTN cell, and the helper counts how many decisions changed anything, not only how many were made. A decision that names a cell with no radio behind it is reported as a decision, not as a handover.

docs.title: System design
docs.text:
Ground segment, space segment and the measured data plane. A1 intents (red) reach the Near-RT RIC directly and the Space RIC over the feeder with a lease. E2 (green) carries KPM up and RC actions down; on the ground path it crosses the feeder link (blue), whose delay follows the live slant range. Dashed boxes are optional or not on the in-simulation path. O1 is not modeled. Script: doc/figures/make_oran_ntn_design.py.

How a control loop runs:

  1. NtnRealStackHelper (from ntn-traffic) stands up an NR NTN cell on an SGP4 orbit: SpectrumPhy, MAC with HARQ and AMC, RLC, PDCP, RRC and EPC. UEs move under TR 38.811 mobility classes.
  2. Per-UE SINR and TBLER are measured on that cell and packed into E2SM-KPM indications under TS 28.552 names. Every KPM row carries its provenance (phy-trace or, for scale-out cells, geometry-budget).
  3. OranNtnE2Node sends each indication one feeder delay up to the Near-RT RIC, optionally aligned to the 100 ms RIC tick. During a feeder outage it buffers them (store and forward) and the Space RIC takes over on board.
  4. xApps decide; the conflict manager resolves contention; the RC action travels one feeder delay back down and reaches a registered actuator, for example NtnRealStackHelper::TriggerHandover or a beam loss model on the live channel.
  5. The next KPM report shows whether the action changed the radio.

docs.title: Results
docs.text: All numbers below come from stored runs. Each figure has a script that reads the raw files, so the plot can be regenerated and checked.

docs.title: Stale A1 intents, lease fallback and control placement under feeder outages
docs.text:
Example oran-ntn-feeder-mgmt, 550 km Walker-Delta shell, 1 to 4 gateways, 6 strategies, 10 seeds each, 1 h simulated per run (240 runs, one binary, sha256 prefix 3232e23199cd6002). Markers are means, bars are 95 % t-intervals over seeds; on log axes the lower whisker is clipped at 10 % of the mean. Data: paper/tnsm-2026-stale-a1-intents/runs.tar.xz (runs/main/) in the toolkit workspace; per-configuration table: doc/figures/oran_ntn_results_summary.csv; script: doc/figures/make_oran_ntn_results.py.

What the campaign shows, at one gateway unless stated (mean ± 95 % interval over 10 seeds):

Strategy Time short of intent Mean age of enforced intent Near-RT deadline misses Ground only 8.27 % ± 1.26 about 0 s 19.57 % ± 1.08 On-board only (intent held without expiry) 5.71 % ± 1.29 6.45 s ± 6.36 0.002 % Reactive hybrid (heartbeat failover) 5.74 % ± 1.26 6.45 s ± 6.39 0.32 % ± 0.02 On-board + lease 3.22 % ± 0.40 0.031 s ± 0.028 0.002 % Reactive + lease 3.26 % ± 0.39 0.031 s ± 0.028 0.33 % ± 0.03 PAL (contact-plan prediction + lease) 3.26 % ± 0.39 0.031 s ± 0.028 0.18 % ± 0.02
  • Stale intents. A satellite that keeps enforcing an A1 intent it cannot refresh holds it for 6.45 s on average at one gateway. Giving the on-board copy a lease, after which it falls back to a safe intent, cuts that age to about 30 ms and the time short of intent from about 5.7 % to about 3.3 %. The lease does the work: on-board, reactive and predictive hosts with the same lease land within each other's intervals.
  • More gateways close the gap. With 3 or 4 gateways the feeder is rarely down, and every strategy sits between 3.3 % and 3.9 %.
  • Control placement. Ground-only near-RT control misses about 19 % of its deadlines with one or two gateways (the feeder delay alone breaks the budget), and still about 2 % with four. Moving near-RT control on board removes almost all misses; contact-plan prediction (PAL) roughly halves the misses of the reactive hybrid, from 0.32 % to 0.18 %.

Scope of this campaign. oran-ntn-feeder-mgmt has no radio stack: cell demand is a stochastic session process and the slice share is a control parameter, not scheduled PRBs. Orbits (SGP4 on Walker elements), feeder visibility and the control plane are real: every E2, A1, heartbeat and lease message is a UDP packet on ns-3 point-to-point links whose delay follows the live slant range. E2AP over SCTP is not simulated. The campaign binary was built from this example plus the default-off campaign options in paper/tnsm-2026-stale-a1-intents/ns3_patch/.

docs.title: Five concurrent xApps on the full constellation scenario
docs.text:
One run of oran-ntn-full-scenario --duration=600 --numUes=20 (seed 1), stored in papers/sim_runs/oran-ntn/run1/ (xapp_metrics.csv, ric_metrics.txt): 71 E2 nodes, 5 xApps, 0 conflicts, 0 policy violations.

xApp Decisions Actions recorded p95 decision latency ho-predict 464 464 0.033 ms beam-hop 2,994 2,994 0.026 ms slice-manager 6 18 0.033 ms doppler-comp 4,272 68,489 0.080 ms tn-ntn-steering 2 2 0.005 ms Total 7,738 71,967

One decision can fan out to many actions, which is why Doppler compensation dominates the action count. In this scenario the RC path records actions; it does not actuate the radio unless the scenario registers an actuator (see Honest scope). The decision latency is xApp computation only, not the end-to-end loop.

docs.title: Honest scope
docs.text:
• Transport. E2 indications and RC actions are delay-modeled simulator events (one feeder delay per direction), the same substitution ns-3 mainline makes for S1-AP and X2-AP. The in-simulation E2 transport is an ns-3 header with toolkit-internal type values, not ASN.1 APER over SCTP.
  • ASN.1 codec. asn1/ holds a hand-written PER codec that round-trips against itself but is not bit-conformant Aligned-PER, so an asn1c peer would not decode it. The FlexRIC listener (flexric-bridge/e2-listener.cc) echoes frame types and does not decode payloads; neither is on the in-simulation control path.
  • Open loop by default. The default RC handler records the decision and returns success. A scenario closes the loop by registering an actuator (SetRcActionCallback, RegisterBeamLossModel, SetHandoverActuator); without one the generic path logs actuated=false.
  • AI. No trained .onnx model ships. Without ONNX Runtime or a model, OranNtnOnnxXapp runs its registered heuristic; IsModelLoaded() says which.
  • Experimental classes. OranNtnGymBeamHop, OranNtnGymPredictive, OranNtnGymSlice, OranNtnGymSteering, the THz xApps and OranNtnMmWaveBeamforming are not yet exercised by any example or test. OranNtnHelper methods SetupMmWaveNtnStack, SetupDualConnectivity, SetupAiIntegration, EnablePhyKpmExtraction, CreateAllAdvancedXapps, SetupIslNetwork, SetupFederatedLearning and GetSatBridge are declared but not implemented; calling them is a link error.
  • O1 is not modeled.

docs.title: satellite - SNS3 (Satellite Network Simulator 3)
docs.text:
satellite is the vendored SNS3 (CNES/Magister) module that ns3-ntn-toolkit builds on for full multi-beam satellite networking in ns-3, providing SatSGP4 orbital mobility, the SatChannel signal-power model, and a complete DVB-S2 forward and DVB-RCS2 return-link protocol stack. Originally developed by Magister Solutions under European Space Agency contract, it is the historical anchor of satellite simulation in ns-3 and is reused unmodified as the toolkit's link-layer and channel base.

Why it matters. Standards-grade non-terrestrial research needs more than a path-loss formula, it needs a real DVB-S2/RCS2 MAC, capacity request signaling, link-budget BLER, and validated orbital propagation. SNS3 supplies all of that as a battle-tested ESA-funded base, so ns3-ntn-toolkit can layer LEO constellations, conditional handover and ray-traced channels on top of a credible satellite stack rather than reinventing it.

docs.title: What it simulates
docs.text:
• SatSGP4 orbital mobility - SatSGP4MobilityModel runs the full SGP4/SDP4 propagator (TLE input) and exposes WGS84/GRS84 geodetic and spherical coordinate systems alongside Cartesian, so satellite, gateway and user-terminal nodes share a consistent earth frame.
  • SatChannel signal-power model - a dedicated SatChannel implements satellite received-signal-power calculation with per-beam channel pairs, channel estimation error containers, and Markov/Loo fading traces.
  • DVB-S2 / DVB-S2X forward link - Time Division Multiplexing BB-frame structure with adaptive coding and modulation across the 16 forward carriers.
  • DVB-RCS2 return link - MF-TDMA with superframe, frame and time-slot scheduling, Return Link Encapsulation, ARQ, and dynamic capacity (RBDC/VBDC) requested from the Network Control Center.
  • Link-results BLER tables - SatLinkResults loads measured BLER-versus-Es/No tables per waveform so PHY decoding reflects real DVB-S2/RCS2 modcod performance rather than an idealized threshold.
  • Multi-beam GEO reference system - a 72 spot-beam, 5-gateway geostationary Ka-band reference network with four-color frequency reuse, plus beam hopping, ESSA, LoRaWAN, inter-satellite link (ISL) routing, and gateway and user-terminal handover.

docs.title: Gallery
docs.text: SNS3 end-to-end architecture: user terminals, satellite, gateways and the Network Control Center.

docs.title: Standards & references
docs.text:
• ETSI DVB-S2 - forward-link Time Division Multiplexing with adaptive coding and modulation.
  • ETSI DVB-S2X - extended modcods and finer granularity on the forward link.
  • ETSI DVB-RCS2 - return-channel MF-TDMA, superframe structure and capacity-request signaling.
  • 3GPP TR 38.811 - non-terrestrial network reference for positioning SNS3 alongside the toolkit's 5G NR NTN channel.
  • AIAA SGP4/SDP4 - orbital propagation from two-line element sets used by SatSGP4MobilityModel.

docs.title: Use cases
docs.text:
• Model a 72-beam GEO Ka-band broadband system with DVB-S2 forward and DVB-RCS2 return links and study end-to-end goodput under realistic BLER.
  • Drive SatSGP4MobilityModel from TLE or constellation ephemeris to simulate LEO satellite passes and beam dynamics.
  • Evaluate DVB-RCS2 dynamic capacity allocation (RBDC/VBDC) under HTTP, CBR or on-off traffic against the NCC scheduler.
  • Study gateway and user-terminal handover and inter-satellite link routing across a multi-satellite topology.
  • Validate link-budget and SINR behavior against the SNS3 link-results tables before layering ray-traced or 5G NR NTN channels on top.

docs.title: Run it
docs.text:
./ns3 run "sat-constellation-example"

This example builds a satellite constellation with SatSGP4 mobility and the SatChannel signal-power model, exercising the DVB-S2/RCS2 stack end to end. Other ready-to-run drivers include sat-cbr-example, sat-link-budget-example, sat-handover-example and sat-fwd-link-beam-hopping-example.

docs.title: thz-ntn
docs.text:
Sub-terahertz and terahertz non-terrestrial links for ns-3, 100 GHz to 1 THz, built on the ITU-R recommendations rather than fitted curves

Toolkit  ·  Docs  ·  Install  ·  Examples  ·  Results

docs.title: Why this module
docs.text:
Above 100 GHz the atmosphere stops being a detail. Molecular absorption, rain, fog and scintillation each move a space-to-ground budget by tens of decibels, and a model that gets one of them wrong by a factor of two still produces a coverage map that looks plausible.

thz-ntn implements each term from its recommendation and says which one: ITU-R P.676-13 Annex 1 line-by-line absorption (44 O2 and 35 H2O lines) integrated over the P.835-6 reference atmospheres, P.838-3 rain, P.840 cloud and fog, and P.618-13 scintillation. On top of the channel it adds ultra-massive MIMO arrays with beam squint, reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS), EKF beam tracking with pointing error, integrated sensing and communication (ISAC), inter-satellite links and alpha-mu fading. The losses enter ns-3 as real PropagationLossModels, so they attenuate packets instead of decorating a CSV.

docs.title: System design
docs.text: Figure 1. Classes and data flow. The atmosphere, weather, antenna and pointing terms feed three consumers: ThzNtnChannelModel for the analytic sweeps, ThzNtnPropagationLossModel chained on the mmwave NR spectrum channel (carrier at most 100 GHz, the limit of the 3GPP model), and ThzNtnLinkErrorModel, which carries IP packets at 300 GHz on a point-to-point link. The RIS can be switched by an xApp through oran-ntn. Source: doc/figures/make_architecture.py.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
The results verify the absorption engine, ThzNtnMolecularAbsorption, which the channel, link-budget and propagation-loss classes all call. They come from a study that swept the engine with the thz-ntn-absorption-sweep example and compared it with a reference: the same P.676-13 Annex 1 kernel and P.835-6 atmospheres integrated along a refracted ray, plus the P.676-13 Annex 2 and P.676-12 approximations. Sweeps, scripts and outputs are in paper/thz-2026-gaseous-absorption/ of the toolkit tree (cpp_sweeps.sh runs the example; analysis.py writes the numbers).

Experiment. Deterministic evaluations on fixed grids, so no random seeds apply. The six P.835-6 atmospheres, each scaled to the precipitable water vapor (PWV) columns from 0.5 to 50 mm that it can hold, give 26 realizable atmospheres; with seven elevations from 10 to 90 degrees they form the operable domain at each window. A Python transcription of the engine reproduced all 88 263 C++ sweep points to a relative difference below 1e-7.

Figure 2. Slant gaseous loss at 30 degrees from Annex 1 (reference) in a dry high-latitude winter atmosphere at 2 mm PWV and in the P.835-6 Section 1.1 atmosphere at 10 mm, with the P.676-13 Annex 2 form (valid to 350 GHz) and the P.676-12 form. Shaded bands mark where each window center was searched.

Figure 3. Largest deviation of each shortcut from the refracted Annex 1 reference at the window centers. (a) Loss over the operable domain; (b) usable bandwidth on the controlled grid. "Module quadrature" is the engine as shipped.

Window center (GHz) 341.5 409.0 464.0 668.5 849.5 Slant loss at 30 degrees, Sec. 1.1 atmosphere, 10 mm PWV (dB) 20.7 39.8 91.5 142.5 174.6 Slant loss at 30 degrees, high-latitude winter, 2 mm PWV (dB) 5.1 10.1 21.7 35.0 43.1 Operable conditions (atmosphere x elevation) 128 88 37 19 12 Check of the engine Largest deviation found Shipped straight-ray quadrature against the refracted reference, all windows, operable domain 0.27 dB Flat-Earth cosecant law against the reference 0.64 dB Regenerated lookup table (data/hitran2024-lut-subthz.csv) against the in-process kernel, within 5 GHz of a window center 0.057 dB (0.74 %) Quadrature raised from 10 to 200 sub-steps per slab 0.02 % Engine against ITU-Rpy at the five centers and 10, 30, 90 degrees 1.0 % Usable bandwidth, any of the geometric shortcuts at most one 0.5 GHz grid step

What the data say: the geometric and numerical simplifications inside the engine cost a fraction of a decibel, while the choice of absorption model does not: the P.676-12 form and a column-only model are off by several to tens of decibels (Figure 3a). Above 600 GHz even the most favorable realizable sea-level atmosphere costs 32.7 dB at 850 GHz and 30 degrees, so the operable domain shrinks quickly with frequency. Against the independent am 14.0 line-by-line model in zenith, P.676-13 lies within 7 % at 340, 410 and 460 GHz and 6 to 18 % higher at 670 and 850 GHz. The same study found and fixed four defects in the engine (a stale lookup-table generator, a table that overrode the configured atmosphere, invented seasonal profiles, a floor on the wrong mixing ratio), each with a regression test. Values are copied from paper/thz-2026-gaseous-absorption/run_all.sh and am_macros.tex.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
Inside the toolkit, where the module is already present and built:

./ns3 run "thz-ntn-absorption-sweep --mode=inproc --elevs=30 --out=sweep.csv"
./ns3 run thz-ntn-leo-ground
./ns3 run "thz-ntn-real-stack --rainMmH=25"

Standalone, into an existing ns-3.43 tree (the GitHub repository of this module is ns3-thz-ntn):

git clone -b thz-ntn-v2 https://github.com/Muhammaduazir69/ns3-thz-ntn.git contrib/thz-ntn
./ns3 configure --enable-examples --enable-tests
./ns3 build

The analytic examples need only the module plus ntn-constellation and ntn-cho for SGP4 geometry; the measured-radio examples build on ntn-traffic and the in-tree mmwave stack. INSTALL.md lists every dependency.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Analytic examples (link budgets and sweeps, no packet data plane; each prints an [analytic-tool] banner):

Example What it shows Command thz-ntn-absorption-sweep Slant gaseous loss over frequency, elevation and PWV; inproc, lut or lutfile engine paths ./ns3 run "thz-ntn-absorption-sweep --mode=lut --pwvs=none" thz-ntn-altitude-relay Absorption avoided by lifting the lower endpoint above the water vapor ./ns3 run thz-ntn-altitude-relay thz-ntn-leo-ground LEO-to-ground sub-THz budget over an SGP4 pass, pass_timeseries.csv ./ns3 run "thz-ntn-leo-ground --freq=300e9" thz-ntn-isl ISL SNR, capacity and Doppler between two SGP4 neighbors ./ns3 run thz-ntn-isl thz-ntn-um-mimo Array gain, DFT codebook and wideband beam squint ./ns3 run "thz-ntn-um-mimo --numElements=128" thz-ntn-ris-assisted Direct against RIS-assisted SNR, N^2 scaling, quantization loss ./ns3 run "thz-ntn-ris-assisted --risSize=64" thz-ntn-dband-constellation D-band UT association on real Walker geometry ./ns3 run thz-ntn-dband-constellation thz-ntn-full-stack Downlink, RIS, ISL, ISAC and EKF tracking together on two SGP4 orbits ./ns3 run thz-ntn-full-stack thz-ntn-demo Eight analytic sections over the module APIs, CSV output ./ns3 run "thz-ntn-demo --example=0"

Packet examples (measured SINR, TBLER and goodput; mmwave NR cell unless noted, carrier at most 100 GHz):

Example What it shows Command thz-ntn-native-300ghz-traffic IP traffic at 300 GHz over Friis plus the module's loss chain on a point-to-point link (no NR PHY, MAC or HARQ) ./ns3 run "thz-ntn-native-300ghz-traffic --freqGhz=300" thz-ntn-real-stack Gaseous absorption and rain chained on the cell; rain applied in the second half ./ns3 run "thz-ntn-real-stack --rainMmH=25" thz-ntn-leo-ground-downlink-traffic Downlink over a receding SGP4 satellite with absorption on real packets ./ns3 run thz-ntn-leo-ground-downlink-traffic thz-ntn-isl-traffic NR link between two cross-plane SGP4 satellites, analytic ISL budget alongside ./ns3 run thz-ntn-isl-traffic thz-ntn-beam-tracking EKF fed by the measured SINR; prediction error becomes a live pointing loss ./ns3 run "thz-ntn-beam-tracking --trackingMode=EKF" thz-ntn-ris-relay-traffic Blockage, then RIS engagement, as live channel events ./ns3 run "thz-ntn-ris-relay-traffic --blockageDb=30" thz-ntn-isac-coexist-traffic ThzNtnIsacScheduler comm share gates the downlink ./ns3 run thz-ntn-isac-coexist-traffic thz-ntn-weather-traffic Fog, rain and snow phases on the live cell ./ns3 run "thz-ntn-weather-traffic --rainMmH=25" thz-ntn-ric-controlled-traffic KPM to oran-ntn; an xApp engages the RIS when SINR drops ./ns3 run "thz-ntn-ric-controlled-traffic --xapp=1"

thz-ntn-isac.cc is kept out of the build (if(FALSE) in examples/CMakeLists.txt) until the ISAC scheduler redesign.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
./test.py -s thz-ntn

The thz-ntn suite (Type::UNIT, 49 test cases) covers FSPL, P.676-13 zenith absorption against reference values, the bundled lookup table (coverage, agreement with the in-process kernel, bypass in a foreign atmosphere), the P.835-6 profiles and WaterVapourScale, P.838-3 coefficients, P.618 rain and scintillation scaling, P.681 LMS, pointing and hardware terms, array gain and codebooks, RIS gain, ISAC range resolution and scheduler modes, NYUSIM calibration, alpha-mu fading, the RIS service model and xApp, and a link budget and error model above 100 GHz. Several cases run under Simulator::Run() (HAPS ascent, rain event, alpha-mu trace).

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text: ns-3.43 core, network, mobility, propagation and spectrum; ntn-constellation and ntn-cho for SGP4 and terminal geometry; ntn-traffic, mmwave and lte for the measured-radio examples; oran-ntn for the RIC-controlled example.

docs.title: Scope and limitations
docs.text:
• The engine integrates a straight ray; the refracted reference differs by at most 0.27 dB at the windows (Results). Spectroscopy is P.676-13, not HITRAN; the lookup table keeps a legacy file name.
  • The NR packet examples are capped at 100 GHz by the in-tree 3GPP spectrum model. Above that, packets run only in thz-ntn-native-300ghz-traffic, which has no NR PHY, MAC or HARQ; read its throughput as link-limited transport.
  • ThzNtnIsacProcessor, ThzNtnIslLink and ThzNtnWaveform have neither an example nor a test. ThzNtnAlphaMuFading, the RIS controller, service model and xApp, the NYUSIM classes and the Itu* reference models are unit-tested but not used by an example.
  • Tesseral orbit terms and terrain are outside this module; geometry comes from ntn-constellation.

docs.title: Standards
docs.text: ITU-R P.676-13 (gaseous attenuation), P.835-6 (reference atmospheres), P.838-3 (rain), P.840 (clouds and fog), P.618-13 (Earth-space propagation, scintillation), P.681-11 (land mobile satellite). 3GPP TR 38.811 and TR 38.821 for NTN geometry, TR 38.901 for the terrestrial baseline.
